statement_summary: The Regulation cites Articles 16 and 114 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union as its legal basis.
evidence_span: Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Articles 16 and 114 thereof

statement_summary: The purpose of the Regulation is stated as improving the functioning of the internal market, promoting human-centric and trustworthy AI and protecting health, safety and fundamental rights against harmful effects of AI systems in the Union while supporting innovation.
evidence_span: The purpose of this Regulation is to improve the functioning of the internal market and promote the uptake of human-centric and trustworthy artificial intelligence (AI)

statement_summary: The Regulation lays down harmonised rules on AI systems, prohibitions, requirements for high-risk systems, transparency rules, rules for general-purpose AI models, rules on market monitoring, surveillance, governance and enforcement, and innovation-support measures.
evidence_span: This Regulation lays down:

statement_summary: The Regulation applies to providers, deployers, importers, distributors, product manufacturers, authorised representatives and affected persons located in the Union, with stated territorial criteria for providers and deployers.
evidence_span: This Regulation applies to:

statement_summary: Product manufacturers who place an AI system on the market or put it into service together with their product and under their own name or trademark are a category to which the Regulation applies.
evidence_span: product manufacturers placing on the market or putting into service an AI system together with their product and under their own name or trademark

statement_summary: Affected persons located in the Union are a category to which the Regulation applies.
evidence_span: affected persons that are located in the Union

statement_summary: For high-risk systems under Article 6(1) related to products in Section B of Annex I, only Articles 6(1), 102 to 109 and 112 apply, and Article 57 applies only where requirements were integrated in that harmonisation legislation.
evidence_span: only Article 6(1), Articles 102 to 109 and Article 112 apply

statement_summary: The Regulation does not apply outside the scope of Union law, does not affect Member State competence on national security, and does not apply to AI systems used exclusively for military, defence or national security purposes.
evidence_span: This Regulation does not apply to areas outside the scope of Union law

statement_summary: The Regulation does not apply to public authorities of a third country or international organisations using AI systems in international law-enforcement or judicial cooperation, provided adequate fundamental-rights safeguards exist.
evidence_span: This Regulation applies neither to public authorities in a third country nor to international organisations

statement_summary: The Regulation does not affect the application of the liability provisions for providers of intermediary services in Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065.
evidence_span: shall not affect the application of the provisions on the liability of providers of intermediary services as set out in Chapter II of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065

statement_summary: The Regulation does not apply to AI systems or models specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development, nor to research, testing or development before placing on the market or putting into service, except testing in real world conditions.
evidence_span: does not apply to AI systems or AI models, including their output, specifically developed and put into service for the sole purpose of scientific research and development

statement_summary: Union data protection law applies to personal data processed in connection with the Regulation, the Regulation does not affect Regulations (EU) 2016/679 and (EU) 2018/1725 or Directives 2002/58/EC and (EU) 2016/680, without prejudice to Articles 10(5) and 59.
evidence_span: Union law on the protection of personal data, privacy and the confidentiality of communications applies to personal data processed in connection with the rights and obligations laid down in this Regulation. This Regulation shall not affect Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or (EU) 2018/1725, or Directive 2002/58/EC or (EU) 2016/680, without prejudice to Article 10(5) and Article 59 of this Regulation

statement_summary: The Regulation is without prejudice to Union rules on consumer protection and product safety and does not apply to obligations of natural persons deploying AI systems in a purely personal non-professional activity.
evidence_span: This Regulation is without prejudice to the rules laid down by other Union legal acts related to consumer protection and product safety

statement_summary: The Regulation does not preclude the Union or Member States from maintaining or introducing rules more favourable to workers regarding AI use by employers, or from encouraging or allowing more favourable collective agreements.
evidence_span: does not preclude the Union or Member States from maintaining or introducing laws, regulations or administrative provisions which are more favourable to workers

statement_summary: The Regulation does not apply to AI systems released under free and open-source licences unless placed on the market or put into service as high-risk AI systems or as systems falling under Article 5 or 50.
evidence_span: does not apply to AI systems released under free and open-source licences

statement_summary: Article 3 states definitions for the purposes of the Regulation.
evidence_span: For the purposes of this Regulation, the following definitions apply:

statement_summary: AI system is defined as a machine-based system designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy that infers from input how to generate outputs that can influence physical or virtual environments.
evidence_span: means a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy and that may exhibit adaptiveness after deployment, and that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments

statement_summary: Provider is defined as a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that develops an AI system or general-purpose AI model, or has one developed, and places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark.
evidence_span: means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model or that has an AI system or a general-purpose AI model developed and places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark, whether for payment or free of charge

statement_summary: Deployer is defined as a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority, except in a personal non-professional activity.
evidence_span: means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority

statement_summary: Authorised representative is defined as a natural or legal person located or established in the Union who has received and accepted a written mandate from a provider to carry out the provider obligations and procedures under the Regulation.
evidence_span: means a natural or legal person located or established in the Union who has received and accepted a written mandate from a provider of an AI system or a general-purpose AI model to, respectively, perform and carry out on its behalf the obligations and procedures established by this Regulation

statement_summary: Importer is defined as a natural or legal person located or established in the Union that places on the market an AI system bearing the name or trademark of a person established in a third country.
evidence_span: means a natural or legal person located or established in the Union that places on the market an AI system that bears the name or trademark

statement_summary: Distributor is defined as a natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the provider or importer, that makes an AI system available on the Union market.
evidence_span: means a natural or legal person in the supply chain, other than the provider or the importer, that makes an AI system available on the Union market

statement_summary: Operator is defined as a provider, product manufacturer, deployer, authorised representative, importer or distributor.
evidence_span: means a provider, product manufacturer, deployer, authorised representative, importer or distributor

statement_summary: Notifying authority is defined as the national authority responsible for setting up and carrying out the procedures for the assessment, designation and notification of conformity assessment bodies and for their monitoring.
evidence_span: means the national authority responsible for setting up and carrying out the necessary procedures for the assessment, designation and notification of conformity assessment bodies and for their monitoring

statement_summary: Conformity assessment body is defined as a body that performs third-party conformity assessment activities, including testing, certification and inspection.
evidence_span: means a body that performs third-party conformity assessment activities, including testing, certification and inspection

statement_summary: Notified body is defined as a conformity assessment body notified in accordance with the Regulation and other relevant Union harmonisation legislation.
evidence_span: means a conformity assessment body notified in accordance with this Regulation and other relevant Union harmonisation legislation

statement_summary: Market surveillance authority is defined as the national authority carrying out the activities and taking the measures pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
evidence_span: means the national authority carrying out the activities and taking the measures pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/1020

statement_summary: Harmonised standard and common specification are defined by reference to Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012.
evidence_span: means a harmonised standard as defined in Article 2(1), point (c), of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012

statement_summary: Special categories of personal data, personal data, non-personal data and profiling are defined by reference to Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Directive (EU) 2016/680 and Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
evidence_span: means the categories of personal data referred to in Article 9(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

statement_summary: Law enforcement authority is defined as any public authority competent for the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or execution of criminal penalties, or any other body entrusted by Member State law to exercise public authority for those purposes.
evidence_span: any public authority competent for the prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or the execution of criminal penalties, including the safeguarding against and the prevention of threats to public security

statement_summary: AI Office is defined as the Commission function of contributing to the implementation, monitoring and supervision of AI systems and general-purpose AI models and AI governance provided for in a Commission Decision of 24 January 2024; references to the AI Office are construed as references to the Commission.
evidence_span: references in this Regulation to the AI Office shall be construed as references to the Commission

statement_summary: National competent authority is defined as a notifying authority or a market surveillance authority; for AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies, references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities are construed as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor.
evidence_span: means a notifying authority or a market surveillance authority; as regards AI systems put into service or used by Union institutions, agencies, offices and bodies, references to national competent authorities or market surveillance authorities in this Regulation shall be construed as references to the European Data Protection Supervisor

statement_summary: AI regulatory sandbox is defined as a controlled framework set up by a competent authority offering providers or prospective providers the possibility to develop, train, validate and test an innovative AI system pursuant to a sandbox plan for a limited time under regulatory supervision; sandbox plan is a document agreed between the participating provider and the competent authority.
evidence_span: means a controlled framework set up by a competent authority which offers providers or prospective providers of AI systems the possibility to develop, train, validate and test, where appropriate in real-world conditions, an innovative AI system, pursuant to a sandbox plan for a limited time under regulatory supervision

statement_summary: Subject (for real-world testing) is defined as a natural person who participates in testing in real-world conditions.
evidence_span: means a natural person who participates in testing in real-world conditions

statement_summary: General-purpose AI model is defined as an AI model displaying significant generality and capable of competently performing a wide range of distinct tasks that can be integrated into downstream systems, except models used for research, development or prototyping before being placed on the market.
evidence_span: means an AI model, including where such an AI model is trained with a large amount of data using self-supervision at scale, that displays significant generality

statement_summary: Downstream provider is defined as a provider of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which integrates an AI model, whether provided by themselves or by another entity under contractual relations.
evidence_span: means a provider of an AI system, including a general-purpose AI system, which integrates an AI model

statement_summary: Providers and deployers shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons operating and using AI systems on their behalf, taking into account knowledge, experience, education, training, context of use and the persons on whom the systems are used.
evidence_span: shall take measures to ensure, to their best extent, a sufficient level of AI literacy of their staff and other persons

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service or use of an AI system deploying subliminal or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques with the objective or effect of materially distorting behaviour and causing or likely causing significant harm is prohibited.
evidence_span: the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that deploys subliminal techniques

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service or use of an AI system exploiting vulnerabilities due to age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with the objective or effect of materially distorting behaviour and causing or likely causing significant harm, is prohibited.
evidence_span: the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of an AI system that exploits any of the vulnerabilities

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service or use of AI systems for social scoring (evaluation or classification of persons over time based on social behaviour or personal characteristics) leading to detrimental treatment in unrelated contexts or unjustified or disproportionate treatment is prohibited.
evidence_span: the placing on the market, the putting into service or the use of AI systems for the evaluation or classification of natural persons

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service for that purpose, or use of an AI system for risk assessment of natural persons to predict criminal offending based solely on profiling or personality traits is prohibited, except systems supporting human assessment based on objective verifiable facts.
evidence_span: the placing on the market, the putting into service for this specific purpose, or the use of an AI system for making risk assessments of natural persons

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service for that purpose, or use of AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage is prohibited.
evidence_span: AI systems that create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service for that purpose, or use of AI systems to infer emotions in workplace and education institutions is prohibited, except for medical or safety reasons.
evidence_span: AI systems to infer emotions of a natural person in the areas of workplace and education institutions

statement_summary: The placing on the market, putting into service for that purpose, or use of biometric categorisation systems that categorise individuals by biometric data to infer race, political opinions, trade union membership, religious or philosophical beliefs, sex life or sexual orientation is prohibited, with stated exceptions for labelling or filtering of lawfully acquired datasets and law enforcement categorisation.
evidence_span: the use of biometric categorisation systems that categorise individually natural persons based on their biometric data

statement_summary: The use of real-time remote biometric identification systems in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement is prohibited unless strictly necessary for listed objectives (targeted search for specific victims and missing persons; prevention of a specific, substantial and imminent threat or terrorist attack; localisation or identification of a suspect of an Annex II offence punishable by at least four years).
evidence_span: publicly accessible spaces for the purposes of law enforcement, unless and in so far as such use is strictly necessary for one of the following objectives

statement_summary: Point (h) of the first subparagraph is without prejudice to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 for the processing of biometric data for other purposes than law enforcement.
evidence_span: is without prejudice to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

statement_summary: Use of real-time remote biometric identification for the Article 5(1)(h) objectives shall be deployed only to confirm the identity of the specifically targeted individual and shall take into account the nature of the situation (seriousness, probability and scale of harm if not used) and the consequences for the rights and freedoms of all persons concerned.
evidence_span: shall be deployed for the purposes set out in that point only to confirm the identity of the specifically targeted individual

statement_summary: Such use shall comply with necessary and proportionate safeguards and conditions under the national law authorising it, and shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment under Article 27 and registered the system in the EU database under Article 49; in urgent cases use may start before registration if registration follows without undue delay.
evidence_span: The use of the ‘real-time’ remote biometric identification system in publicly accessible spaces shall be authorised only if the law enforcement authority has completed a fundamental rights impact assessment

statement_summary: Each law-enforcement use of real-time remote biometric identification is subject to prior authorisation by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding, issued upon reasoned request under national rules, only where satisfied on objective evidence or clear indications that the use is necessary and proportionate and limited in time and scope.
evidence_span: shall be subject to a prior authorisation granted by a judicial authority or an independent administrative authority whose decision is binding

statement_summary: If authorisation is rejected, use shall be stopped with immediate effect and all data, results and outputs of that use shall be immediately discarded and deleted.
evidence_span: If such authorisation is rejected, the use shall be stopped with immediate effect

statement_summary: No decision that produces an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken based solely on the output of the real-time remote biometric identification system.
evidence_span: No decision that produces an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken based solely on the output

statement_summary: Each use of a real-time remote biometric identification system for law enforcement shall be notified to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority in accordance with national rules, containing at least the information specified under paragraph 6 and no sensitive operational data.
evidence_span: shall be notified to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority

statement_summary: A Member State may decide to provide for the possibility to fully or partially authorise real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement within the limits of Article 5(1)(h), (2) and (3), and may introduce more restrictive laws in accordance with Union law.
evidence_span: A Member State may decide to provide for the possibility to fully or partially authorise the use

statement_summary: Market surveillance authorities and national data protection authorities notified of uses under paragraph 4 shall submit annual reports on such use to the Commission, and the Commission shall provide Member States and those authorities with a reporting template.
evidence_span: shall submit to the Commission annual reports on such use

statement_summary: The Commission shall publish annual reports on the use of real-time remote biometric identification systems for law enforcement based on aggregated data in Member States, excluding sensitive operational data.
evidence_span: The Commission shall publish annual reports on the use of real-time remote biometric identification systems

statement_summary: Article 5 does not affect prohibitions that apply where an AI practice infringes other Union law.
evidence_span: This Article shall not affect the prohibitions that apply where an AI practice infringes other Union law

statement_summary: An AI system is considered high-risk where it is a safety component of, or is itself, a product covered by the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I and that product must undergo third-party conformity assessment under that legislation.
evidence_span: that AI system shall be considered to be high-risk where both of the following conditions are fulfilled

statement_summary: AI systems referred to in Annex III are considered high-risk, except where they pose no significant risk of harm (including by not materially influencing decision making) under the listed conditions, and always where they perform profiling of natural persons.
evidence_span: AI systems referred to in Annex III shall be considered to be high-risk

statement_summary: A provider who considers that an Annex III system is not high-risk shall document its assessment before placing on the market or putting into service, is subject to the registration obligation of Article 49(2), and shall provide the documentation upon request of national competent authorities.
evidence_span: shall document its assessment before that system is placed on the market or put into service

statement_summary: The Commission shall, after consulting the European Artificial Intelligence Board and no later than 2 February 2026, provide guidelines specifying the practical implementation of Article 6 in line with Article 96 together with a list of practical examples of high-risk and not high-risk use cases.
evidence_span: The Commission shall, after consulting the European Artificial Intelligence Board

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered (and shall) to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend the conditions of Article 6(3) second subparagraph by adding, modifying or deleting conditions on specified evidence, and any amendment shall not decrease the overall level of protection and shall ensure consistency with Article 7(1) delegated acts.
evidence_span: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend paragraph 3, second subparagraph

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend Annex III by adding or modifying high-risk use cases where the systems are intended for an Annex III area and pose a risk of harm equivalent to or greater than systems already listed.
evidence_span: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to amend Annex III by adding or modifying use-cases

statement_summary: When assessing the risk condition, the Commission shall take into account listed criteria (intended purpose, extent of use, data processed, autonomy, past harm, extent of harm, dependency, power imbalance, reversibility, benefit, and existing Union law redress and risk-minimising measures).
evidence_span: the Commission shall take into account the following criteria

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to remove high-risk AI systems from Annex III where they no longer pose significant risks and deletion does not decrease the overall level of protection.
evidence_span: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to amend the list in Annex III by removing high-risk AI systems

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems shall comply with the requirements of Section 2 taking into account intended purpose and the generally acknowledged state of the art, with the Article 9 risk management system taken into account; the text names the systems, not an operator position, as addressee.
evidence_span: High-risk AI systems shall comply with the requirements laid down in this Section

statement_summary: Where a product contains an AI system subject to this Regulation and to Annex I Section A legislation, providers are responsible for full compliance of the product with all applicable Union harmonisation legislation and may integrate testing, reporting, information and documentation into existing documentation and procedures required under that legislation.
evidence_span: providers shall be responsible for ensuring that their product is fully compliant with all applicable requirements

statement_summary: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained for high-risk AI systems as a continuous iterative lifecycle process comprising identification, estimation, evaluation of risks and adoption of targeted risk management measures, with residual risk judged acceptable, testing against predefined metrics before placing on the market, and optional real-world testing under Article 60; the paragraphs do not name an obligor.
evidence_span: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems

statement_summary: When implementing the risk management system providers shall give consideration to whether the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under 18 and, as appropriate, other vulnerable groups.
evidence_span: providers shall give consideration to whether in view of its intended purpose the high-risk AI system is likely to have an adverse impact on persons under the age of 18

statement_summary: For providers subject to internal risk management requirements under other Union law, the aspects in Article 9(1) to (9) may be part of or combined with the procedures under that law.
evidence_span: may be part of, or combined with, the risk management procedures established pursuant to that law

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems using training of AI models shall be developed on training, validation and testing data sets subject to data governance and management practices and meeting quality criteria (relevance, representativeness, freedom from errors, completeness, statistical properties, setting-specific characteristics); for systems not using training techniques, the criteria apply to testing data sets; the paragraphs name no obligor.
evidence_span: shall be developed on the basis of training, validation and testing data sets that meet the quality criteria

statement_summary: Providers may exceptionally process special categories of personal data to the extent strictly necessary for bias detection and correction, subject to appropriate safeguards and, in addition to data protection law, all listed conditions (no effective alternative, technical limitation on re-use, security and access controls, no transmission to other parties, deletion, documentation in records of processing).
evidence_span: the providers of such systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data

statement_summary: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before placing on the market or putting into service and kept up to date, and for products under Annex I Section A legislation a single set of technical documentation shall be drawn up containing the information of this Article and of those acts; no obligor is named.
evidence_span: The technical documentation of a high-risk AI system shall be drawn up before that system is placed on the market or put into service

statement_summary: Technical documentation shall demonstrate compliance and give national competent authorities and notified bodies the information needed to assess it, containing at least the Annex IV elements; SMEs may provide Annex IV elements in a simplified manner using a Commission-established simplified form targeted at small and microenterprises, and notified bodies shall accept the form for conformity assessment.
evidence_span: SMEs, including start-ups, may provide the elements of the technical documentation specified in Annex IV in a simplified manner

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend Annex IV where necessary so that technical documentation provides the information necessary to assess compliance in light of technical progress.
evidence_span: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend Annex IV

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow automatic recording of events (logs) over their lifetime, enabling traceability relevant for risk situations, post-market monitoring and monitoring of operation, with specified minimum logging for Annex III point 1(a) systems; no obligor is named.
evidence_span: High-risk AI systems shall technically allow for the automatic recording of events (logs) over the lifetime of the system

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems shall be designed so that operation is sufficiently transparent for deployers to interpret output, and shall be accompanied by instructions for use with concise, complete, correct and clear information containing at least provider identity and contact details, characteristics, capabilities and limitations, pre-determined changes, human oversight measures, resource needs and log-collection mechanisms.
evidence_span: High-risk AI systems shall be accompanied by instructions for use

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems shall be designed with appropriate human-machine interface tools so that natural persons can effectively oversee them; oversight measures are commensurate with risks and are either built into the system by the provider or identified by the provider as appropriate for implementation by the deployer, and the system shall be provided to the deployer so that persons assigned oversight can understand, monitor, remain aware of automation bias, interpret, decide not to use or override, and intervene or stop.
evidence_span: measures identified by the provider before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service and that are appropriate to be implemented by the deployer

statement_summary: For high-risk systems under Annex III point 1(a), the oversight measures shall ensure that no action or decision is taken by the deployer on the basis of the identification unless separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons with the necessary competence, training and authority, except where Union or national law considers this disproportionate for law enforcement, migration, border control or asylum.
evidence_span: no action or decision is taken by the deployer on the basis of the identification resulting from the system unless that identification has been separately verified and confirmed by at least two natural persons

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems shall be designed to achieve appropriate accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle, with accuracy levels declared in the instructions for use, resilience against errors, faults and unauthorised third-party attempts, redundancy and feedback-loop mitigation; no obligor is named.
evidence_span: High-risk AI systems shall be designed and developed in such a way that they achieve an appropriate level of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity

statement_summary: The Commission shall, in cooperation with relevant stakeholders and organisations such as metrology and benchmarking authorities, encourage as appropriate the development of benchmarks and measurement methodologies for measuring accuracy and robustness.
evidence_span: the Commission shall, in cooperation with relevant stakeholders and organisations such as metrology and benchmarking authorities, encourage, as appropriate, the development of benchmarks and measurement methodologies

statement_summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall ensure that their systems are compliant with the requirements set out in Section 2.
evidence_span: ensure that their high-risk AI systems are compliant with the requirements set out in Section 2

statement_summary: Providers shall indicate on the high-risk AI system, its packaging or accompanying documentation their name, registered trade name or trade mark and contact address.
evidence_span: indicate on the high-risk AI system or, where that is not possible, on its packaging or its accompanying documentation

statement_summary: Providers shall have a quality management system in place which complies with Article 17.
evidence_span: have a quality management system in place which complies with Article 17

statement_summary: Providers shall keep the documentation referred to in Article 18 and, when under their control, the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems as referred to in Article 19.
evidence_span: keep the documentation referred to in Article 18

statement_summary: Providers shall ensure that the high-risk AI system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment procedure under Article 43 prior to placing on the market or putting into service.
evidence_span: ensure that the high-risk AI system undergoes the relevant conformity assessment procedure as referred to in Article 43

statement_summary: Providers shall draw up an EU declaration of conformity under Article 47 and affix the CE marking to the system, packaging or documentation under Article 48.
evidence_span: draw up an EU declaration of conformity in accordance with Article 47

statement_summary: Providers shall comply with the registration obligations in Article 49(1) and take necessary corrective actions and provide information as required in Article 20.
evidence_span: comply with the registration obligations referred to in Article 49(1)

statement_summary: Providers shall, upon a reasoned request of a national competent authority, demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements of Section 2.
evidence_span: upon a reasoned request of a national competent authority, demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system

statement_summary: Providers shall ensure that the high-risk AI system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882.
evidence_span: ensure that the high-risk AI system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882

statement_summary: Providers shall put a documented quality management system in place that ensures compliance, covering at least regulatory compliance strategy, design, development and quality control, testing and validation, technical specifications and standards, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, serious incident reporting, communication with authorities and other parties, record-keeping, resource management and an accountability framework of management and staff responsibilities, proportionate to the size of the provider.
evidence_span: shall put a quality management system in place that ensures compliance with this Regulation

statement_summary: Providers subject to quality management obligations under relevant sectoral Union law may include the Article 17(1) aspects as part of the systems under that law.
evidence_span: may include the aspects listed in paragraph 1 as part of the quality management systems pursuant to that law

statement_summary: For providers that are financial institutions subject to internal governance requirements under Union financial services law, the quality management system obligation (except Article 17(1) points (g), (h), (i)) is deemed fulfilled by complying with those internal governance rules, taking harmonised standards of Article 40 into account.
evidence_span: shall be deemed to be fulfilled by complying with the rules on internal governance arrangements or processes

statement_summary: For ten years after placing on the market or putting into service, the provider shall keep at the disposal of the national competent authorities the technical documentation, quality management system documentation, changes approved by notified bodies, notified body decisions and documents, and the EU declaration of conformity.
evidence_span: shall, for a period ending 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service, keep at the disposal of the national competent authorities

statement_summary: Each Member State shall determine conditions under which the documentation remains at the disposal of national competent authorities where a provider or its authorised representative established on its territory goes bankrupt or ceases activity before the end of the period.
evidence_span: Each Member State shall determine conditions under which the documentation referred to in paragraph 1 remains at the disposal

statement_summary: Providers that are financial institutions shall maintain the technical documentation as part of the documentation kept under the relevant Union financial services law.
evidence_span: shall maintain the technical documentation as part of the documentation kept under the relevant Union financial services law

statement_summary: Providers shall keep the automatically generated logs under their control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and at least six months unless otherwise provided in applicable Union or national law.
evidence_span: shall keep the logs referred to in Article 12(1), automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems

statement_summary: Providers that are financial institutions shall maintain the automatically generated logs as part of the documentation kept under the relevant financial services law.
evidence_span: shall maintain the logs automatically generated by their high-risk AI systems as part of the documentation kept under the relevant financial services law

statement_summary: Providers who consider or have reason to consider that a high-risk AI system they placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity shall immediately take corrective actions to bring it into conformity, withdraw, disable or recall it, and inform the distributors and, where applicable, the deployers, the authorised representative and importers.
evidence_span: shall immediately take the necessary corrective actions to bring that system into conformity, to withdraw it, to disable it, or to recall it

statement_summary: Where the system presents a risk within the meaning of Article 79(1), the provider shall immediately investigate causes in collaboration with the reporting deployer where applicable, and inform the competent market surveillance authorities and, where applicable, the notified body that issued a certificate, of the nature of the non-compliance and corrective action taken.
evidence_span: it shall immediately investigate the causes, in collaboration with the reporting deployer, where applicable

statement_summary: Providers shall, upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, provide that authority all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity with Section 2, in a language easily understood by the authority.
evidence_span: upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, provide that authority all the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the conformity

statement_summary: Upon reasoned request providers shall also give the requesting competent authority access to the automatically generated logs under their control.
evidence_span: providers shall also give the requesting competent authority, as applicable, access to the automatically generated logs

statement_summary: Any information obtained by a competent authority pursuant to Article 21 shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations of Article 78.
evidence_span: shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78

statement_summary: Before making high-risk AI systems available on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall by written mandate appoint an authorised representative established in the Union and shall enable it to perform the tasks in the mandate; the mandate shall empower the representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by competent authorities on all issues of compliance.
evidence_span: providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union

statement_summary: The authorised representative shall perform the tasks in the mandate, provide a copy of the mandate to market surveillance authorities on request, and the mandate shall empower it to verify the EU declaration of conformity, technical documentation and conformity assessment, keep documents at the disposal of authorities for ten years, provide information and log access on reasoned request, cooperate with authorities, and comply with registration obligations.
evidence_span: The authorised representative shall perform the tasks specified in the mandate received from the provider

statement_summary: The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations, and shall immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority and, where applicable, the relevant notified body of the termination and the reasons.
evidence_span: The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations

statement_summary: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, importers shall ensure conformity by verifying that the provider has carried out the conformity assessment procedure and drawn up the technical documentation, that the system bears the CE marking and is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use, and that the provider has appointed an authorised representative.
evidence_span: importers shall ensure that the system is in conformity with this Regulation by verifying that

statement_summary: An importer with sufficient reason to consider a high-risk AI system non-conforming, falsified or accompanied by falsified documentation shall not place it on the market until conformity, and shall inform the provider, the authorised representative and the market surveillance authorities where the system presents a risk under Article 79(1).
evidence_span: it shall not place the system on the market until it has been brought into conformity

statement_summary: Importers shall indicate their name, trade name or mark and address on the system and its packaging or documentation, ensure that storage or transport conditions do not jeopardise compliance, and keep for ten years a copy of the notified body certificate, instructions for use and EU declaration of conformity.
evidence_span: Importers shall indicate their name, registered trade name or registered trade mark, and the address at which they can be contacted

statement_summary: Importers shall provide the relevant competent authorities, upon reasoned request, with all necessary information and documentation to demonstrate conformity in an easily understood language, ensure the technical documentation can be made available, and cooperate with the relevant competent authorities in actions concerning systems they placed on the market.
evidence_span: Importers shall provide the relevant competent authorities, upon a reasoned request, with all the necessary information and documentation

statement_summary: Before making a high-risk AI system available, distributors shall verify that it bears the CE marking, is accompanied by a copy of the EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use, and that the provider and importer have complied with their obligations under Article 16 points (b) and (c) and Article 23(3).
evidence_span: distributors shall verify that it bears the required CE marking

statement_summary: A distributor that considers or has reason to consider a system non-conforming shall not make it available until conformity and, where a risk under Article 79(1) arises, shall inform the provider or importer.
evidence_span: it shall not make the high-risk AI system available on the market until the system has been brought into conformity

statement_summary: Distributors shall ensure that storage or transport conditions under their responsibility do not jeopardise compliance of the system with Section 2.
evidence_span: Distributors shall ensure that, while a high-risk AI system is under their responsibility, storage or transport conditions

statement_summary: A distributor that considers a system it has made available non-conforming shall take corrective actions, withdraw or recall it, or ensure that the provider, importer or any relevant operator does so, and where a risk under Article 79(1) exists shall immediately inform the provider or importer and the competent authorities, giving details of the non-compliance and corrective actions.
evidence_span: shall take the corrective actions necessary to bring that system into conformity with those requirements, to withdraw it or recall it

statement_summary: Distributors shall, upon reasoned request, provide the relevant competent authority with the information and documentation regarding their actions needed to demonstrate conformity, and cooperate with relevant competent authorities in actions concerning systems they made available.
evidence_span: distributors of a high-risk AI system shall provide that authority with all the information and documentation regarding their actions

statement_summary: Any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party shall be considered a provider of a high-risk AI system and subject to the provider obligations under Article 16 where it puts its name or trademark on a high-risk AI system already on the market, makes a substantial modification that leaves it high-risk, or modifies the intended purpose of a non-high-risk AI system so that it becomes high-risk.
evidence_span: shall be considered to be a provider of a high-risk AI system for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the provider under Article 16

statement_summary: Where the Article 25(1) circumstances occur, the provider that initially placed the system on the market or put it into service is no longer considered the provider of that system and shall closely cooperate with new providers, making available necessary information, reasonably expected technical access and other assistance, unless it clearly specified that its system is not to be changed into a high-risk AI system.
evidence_span: That initial provider shall closely cooperate with new providers and shall make available the necessary information

statement_summary: For high-risk AI systems that are safety components of products under Annex I Section A legislation, the product manufacturer shall be considered the provider and subject to Article 16 obligations where the system is placed on the market together with the product under its name or trademark, or put into service under its name or trademark after the product has been placed on the market.
evidence_span: the product manufacturer shall be considered to be the provider of the high-risk AI system, and shall be subject to the obligations under Article 16

statement_summary: The provider of a high-risk AI system and the third party supplying AI systems, tools, services, components or processes used or integrated in it shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and assistance to enable the provider to comply, except for third parties making tools, services, processes or components other than general-purpose AI models accessible under a free and open-source licence.
evidence_span: shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance

statement_summary: The AI Office (construed as the Commission) may develop and recommend voluntary model terms for contracts between providers of high-risk AI systems and third-party suppliers, shall take into account sectoral or business-case contractual requirements, and the terms shall be published free of charge in an easily usable electronic format.
evidence_span: The AI Office may develop and recommend voluntary model terms for contracts between providers of high-risk AI systems and third parties

statement_summary: Article 25(2) and (3) are without prejudice to the need to observe and protect intellectual property rights, confidential business information and trade secrets.
evidence_span: are without prejudice to the need to observe and protect intellectual property rights

statement_summary: Deployers of high-risk AI systems shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use, without prejudice to other deployer obligations and to the deployer freedom to organise its own resources and activities for implementing the human oversight measures indicated by the provider.
evidence_span: shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure they use such systems in accordance with the instructions for use

statement_summary: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority, as well as the necessary support.
evidence_span: Deployers shall assign human oversight to natural persons who have the necessary competence, training and authority

statement_summary: To the extent the deployer exercises control over the input data, it shall ensure that the input data is relevant and sufficiently representative in view of the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system.
evidence_span: that deployer shall ensure that input data is relevant and sufficiently representative

statement_summary: Deployers shall monitor the operation of the system on the basis of the instructions for use and inform providers where relevant under Article 72; where they have reason to consider a risk under Article 79(1) they shall without undue delay inform the provider or distributor and the market surveillance authority and suspend use; where they identify a serious incident they shall immediately inform first the provider, then the importer or distributor and the market surveillance authorities, with Article 73 applying mutatis mutandis if the provider cannot be reached, excluding sensitive operational data of law enforcement deployers.
evidence_span: Deployers shall monitor the operation of the high-risk AI system on the basis of the instructions for use

statement_summary: For deployers that are financial institutions subject to internal governance requirements under Union financial services law, the monitoring obligation is deemed fulfilled by complying with those governance rules.
evidence_span: shall be deemed to be fulfilled by complying with the rules on internal governance arrangements, processes and mechanisms

statement_summary: Deployers shall keep the logs automatically generated by the system under their control for a period appropriate to the intended purpose and at least six months unless otherwise provided in applicable Union or national law; deployers that are financial institutions shall maintain the logs as part of documentation kept under financial services law.
evidence_span: shall keep the logs automatically generated by that high-risk AI system to the extent such logs are under their control

statement_summary: Before putting into service or using a high-risk AI system at the workplace, deployers who are employers shall inform workers representatives and the affected workers that they will be subject to its use, in accordance with Union and national rules on information of workers.
evidence_span: deployers who are employers shall inform workers’ representatives and the affected workers

statement_summary: Deployers that are public authorities or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies shall comply with the registration obligations of Article 49 and shall not use a system they find not registered in the EU database of Article 71, informing the provider or distributor.
evidence_span: shall comply with the registration obligations referred to in Article 49

statement_summary: Where applicable, deployers shall use the information provided under Article 13 to comply with their obligation to carry out a data protection impact assessment under Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680.
evidence_span: shall use the information provided under Article 13 of this Regulation to comply with their obligation to carry out a data protection impact assessment

statement_summary: In an investigation for the targeted search of a person suspected or convicted of a criminal offence, the deployer of a high-risk post-remote biometric identification system shall request an authorisation, ex ante or without undue delay and within 48 hours, by a judicial authority or an administrative authority whose decision is binding and subject to judicial review, except for initial identification of a potential suspect based on objective and verifiable facts; each use is limited to what is strictly necessary for a specific criminal offence.
evidence_span: the deployer of a high-risk AI system for post-remote biometric identification shall request an authorisation

statement_summary: If the requested authorisation is rejected, use of the post-remote biometric identification system linked to it shall be stopped with immediate effect and the personal data linked to the use shall be deleted.
evidence_span: the use of the post-remote biometric identification system linked to that requested authorisation shall be stopped with immediate effect

statement_summary: Post-remote biometric identification systems shall in no case be used for law enforcement in an untargeted way without any link to a criminal offence, criminal proceeding, genuine threat of an offence or the search for a specific missing person, and no decision producing an adverse legal effect on a person may be taken by law enforcement authorities based solely on the output.
evidence_span: In no case shall such high-risk AI system for post-remote biometric identification be used for law enforcement purposes in an untargeted way

statement_summary: Regardless of purpose or deployer, each use of such systems shall be documented in the relevant police file and made available to the relevant market surveillance authority and the national data protection authority upon request, excluding sensitive operational data, without prejudice to powers conferred by Directive (EU) 2016/680.
evidence_span: each use of such high-risk AI systems shall be documented in the relevant police file

statement_summary: Deployers shall submit annual reports to the relevant market surveillance and national data protection authorities on their use of post-remote biometric identification systems, excluding sensitive operational data; the reports may be aggregated.
evidence_span: Deployers shall submit annual reports to the relevant market surveillance and national data protection authorities

statement_summary: Member States may introduce, in accordance with Union law, more restrictive laws on the use of post-remote biometric identification systems.
evidence_span: Member States may introduce, in accordance with Union law, more restrictive laws on the use of post-remote biometric identification systems

statement_summary: Without prejudice to Article 50, deployers of Annex III high-risk AI systems that make or assist in decisions related to natural persons shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the system, and Article 13 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 applies to law-enforcement use.
evidence_span: shall inform the natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system

statement_summary: Deployers shall cooperate with the relevant competent authorities in any action those authorities take in relation to the high-risk AI system in order to implement the Regulation.
evidence_span: Deployers shall cooperate with the relevant competent authorities in any action those authorities take

statement_summary: Prior to deploying an Article 6(2) high-risk AI system (except the area in point 2 of Annex III), deployers that are bodies governed by public law or private entities providing public services, and deployers of systems in points 5(b) and (c) of Annex III, shall assess the impact on fundamental rights, covering processes of use, period and frequency of use, categories of persons likely affected, specific risks of harm, human oversight implementation and measures if risks materialise.
evidence_span: shall perform an assessment of the impact on fundamental rights that the use of such system may produce

statement_summary: The fundamental rights impact assessment obligation applies to the first use; the deployer may rely on previous or provider-conducted assessments in similar cases and shall update the information if elements change or are no longer up to date.
evidence_span: The obligation laid down in paragraph 1 applies to the first use of the high-risk AI system

statement_summary: Once the assessment has been performed, the deployer shall notify the market surveillance authority of its results, submitting the filled-out template as part of the notification; in the case of Article 46(1) deployers may be exempt.
evidence_span: the deployer shall notify the market surveillance authority of its results

statement_summary: If any obligation of Article 27 is already met through the data protection impact assessment under Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Article 27 of Directive (EU) 2016/680, the fundamental rights impact assessment shall complement that assessment.
evidence_span: the fundamental rights impact assessment referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article shall complement that data protection impact assessment

statement_summary: The AI Office (construed as the Commission) shall develop a template for a questionnaire, including through an automated tool, to facilitate deployers in complying with Article 27 in a simplified manner.
evidence_span: The AI Office shall develop a template for a questionnaire, including through an automated tool

statement_summary: Each Member State shall designate or establish at least one notifying authority responsible for setting up and carrying out the procedures for assessment, designation and notification of conformity assessment bodies and for their monitoring, with the procedures developed in cooperation between the notifying authorities of all Member States.
evidence_span: Each Member State shall designate or establish at least one notifying authority

statement_summary: Member States may decide that the assessment and monitoring of conformity assessment bodies is carried out by a national accreditation body within the meaning of, and in accordance with, Regulation (EC) No 765/2008.
evidence_span: Member States may decide that the assessment and monitoring referred to in paragraph 1 is to be carried out by a national accreditation body

statement_summary: Notifying authorities shall be established, organised and operated so that no conflict of interest arises with conformity assessment bodies and objectivity and impartiality are safeguarded, shall take notification decisions by competent persons different from those who assessed the bodies, and shall offer neither activities that conformity assessment bodies perform nor commercial consultancy services.
evidence_span: Notifying authorities shall be established, organised and operated in such a way that no conflict of interest arises with conformity assessment bodies

statement_summary: Notifying authorities shall safeguard the confidentiality of information obtained in accordance with Article 78 and shall have an adequate number of competent personnel with the necessary expertise, including in information technologies, AI, law and the supervision of fundamental rights.
evidence_span: Notifying authorities shall safeguard the confidentiality of the information that they obtain, in accordance with Article 78

statement_summary: Conformity assessment bodies shall submit an application for notification to the notifying authority of the Member State in which they are established, accompanied by a description of activities, modules and AI system types, an accreditation certificate issued by a national accreditation body where one exists, and valid documents on other Union harmonisation designations, or otherwise all documentary evidence necessary for verification, recognition and regular monitoring of compliance with Article 31.
evidence_span: Conformity assessment bodies shall submit an application for notification to the notifying authority of the Member State in which they are established

statement_summary: Notified bodies designated under other Union harmonisation legislation may use documents linked to those designations to support designation under this Regulation, and the notified body shall update the documentation whenever relevant changes occur so that the authority responsible for notified bodies can monitor and verify continuous compliance with Article 31.
evidence_span: The notified body shall update the documentation referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article whenever relevant changes occur

statement_summary: Notifying authorities may notify only conformity assessment bodies which have satisfied the requirements laid down in Article 31.
evidence_span: Notifying authorities may notify only conformity assessment bodies which have satisfied the requirements laid down in Article 31

statement_summary: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission, of each conformity assessment body, including full details of activities, modules, AI system types and attestation of competence, or documentary evidence of competence and monitoring arrangements where not based on an accreditation certificate.
evidence_span: Notifying authorities shall notify the Commission and the other Member States, using the electronic notification tool developed and managed by the Commission

statement_summary: The conformity assessment body may perform notified body activities only where no objections are raised by the Commission or the other Member States within two weeks of a notification including an accreditation certificate or two months where documentary evidence is included; where objections are raised the Commission shall without delay consult the relevant Member States and the body, decide whether the authorisation is justified and address its decision to the Member State concerned and the body.
evidence_span: may perform the activities of a notified body only where no objections are raised by the Commission or the other Member States

statement_summary: A notified body shall be established under the national law of a Member State and shall have legal personality.
evidence_span: A notified body shall be established under the national law of a Member State and shall have legal personality

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall satisfy organisational, quality management, resource, process and cybersecurity requirements, an organisational structure, allocation of responsibilities and reporting lines that ensure confidence in their performance, procedures that take due account of provider size, sector, structure and system complexity, capability to carry out all tasks with the highest professional integrity and competence, and sufficient internal competences and permanent personnel.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall satisfy the organisational, quality management, resources and process requirements

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall be independent of the provider of the assessed high-risk AI system, of any other operator having an economic interest in it and of competitors of the provider, and shall be organised and operated to safeguard independence, objectivity and impartiality with a documented structure and procedures.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall be independent of the provider of a high-risk AI system in relation to which they perform conformity assessment activities

statement_summary: Neither a conformity assessment body, its top-level management nor the personnel responsible for conformity assessment tasks shall be directly involved in the design, development, marketing or use of high-risk AI systems nor represent the parties engaged in those activities, nor engage in any activity that might conflict with their independence of judgement or integrity, in particular consultancy services.
evidence_span: Neither a conformity assessment body, its top-level management nor the personnel responsible for carrying out its conformity assessment tasks shall be directly involved

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall have documented procedures ensuring confidentiality under Article 78 with staff bound by professional secrecy except in relation to the notifying authorities of the Member State, and shall take out appropriate liability insurance unless liability is assumed by the Member State.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall have documented procedures in place ensuring that their personnel, committees, subsidiaries, subcontractors

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall participate in coordination activities referred to in Article 38 and shall take part directly in, or be represented in, European standardisation organisations, or ensure that they are aware and up to date in respect of relevant standards.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall participate in coordination activities as referred to in Article 38

statement_summary: Article 26(10) is without prejudice to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2016/680 for the processing of biometric data.
evidence_span: is without prejudice to Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and Article 10 of Directive (EU) 2016/680

statement_summary: A conformity assessment body demonstrating conformity with the criteria of relevant harmonised standards published in the Official Journal is presumed to comply with the requirements of Article 31 in so far as the standards cover those requirements.
evidence_span: it shall be presumed to comply with the requirements set out in Article 31 in so far as the applicable harmonised standards cover those requirements

statement_summary: Where a notified body subcontracts tasks or has recourse to a subsidiary it shall ensure they meet the Article 31 requirements, inform the notifying authority, take full responsibility, subcontract only with the agreement of the provider, publish a list of subsidiaries, and keep assessment documents at the disposal of the notifying authority for five years after termination of subcontracting.
evidence_span: it shall ensure that the subcontractor or the subsidiary meets the requirements laid down in Article 31, and shall inform the notifying authority accordingly

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall verify the conformity of high-risk AI systems per Article 43 avoiding unnecessary burdens for providers and respecting the required degree of rigour, and shall make available and submit upon request all relevant documentation, including providers documentation, to the notifying authority so that it can conduct its assessment, designation, notification and monitoring.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall verify the conformity of high-risk AI systems in accordance with the conformity assessment procedures set out in Article 43

statement_summary: The Commission shall assign a single identification number to each notified body and shall make publicly available and keep up to date the list of notified bodies with their numbers and the activities for which they have been notified.
evidence_span: The Commission shall assign a single identification number to each notified body

statement_summary: The notifying authority shall notify the Commission and other Member States of relevant changes to a notification via the electronic notification tool; the procedures of Articles 29 and 30 apply to extensions of scope and paragraphs 3 to 9 to other changes.
evidence_span: The notifying authority shall notify the Commission and the other Member States of any relevant changes to the notification of a notified body

statement_summary: A notified body deciding to cease conformity assessment activities shall inform the notifying authority and the providers concerned as soon as possible and at least one year in advance for a planned cessation; certificates may remain valid for nine months if another notified body confirms in writing it will assume responsibility, which shall complete a full assessment before issuing new certificates; where the body has ceased the notifying authority shall withdraw the designation.
evidence_span: it shall inform the notifying authority and the providers concerned as soon as possible

statement_summary: Where a notifying authority has sufficient reason to consider that a notified body no longer meets Article 31 requirements or fails its obligations, it shall investigate without delay, inform the body of the objections and give it the possibility to make its views known, restrict, suspend or withdraw the designation depending on seriousness, and immediately inform the Commission and the other Member States; the notified body shall inform the providers concerned within 10 days of a suspension, restriction or withdrawal.
evidence_span: the notifying authority shall without delay investigate the matter with the utmost diligence

statement_summary: In the event of restriction, suspension or withdrawal of a designation the notifying authority shall keep the notified body files and make them available to notifying authorities of other Member States and market surveillance authorities on request, assess the impact on certificates, report to the Commission and other Member States within three months, require the notified body to suspend or withdraw unduly issued certificates, inform the Commission and Member States about them, and provide the national competent authorities where the provider has its place of business with the relevant information.
evidence_span: the notifying authority shall take appropriate steps to ensure that the files of the notified body concerned are kept

statement_summary: Except for unduly issued certificates, certificates remain valid after suspension or restriction of a designation if the notifying authority confirms no risk and outlines remedy timelines, or confirms that no relevant certificates will be issued and, where it finds the notified body unable to support existing certificates, the provider confirms in writing to the national competent authorities within three months that another notified body is temporarily assuming the functions; after withdrawal certificates remain valid for nine months if the national competent authority confirms no risk and another notified body confirms in writing that it assumes responsibility; the national competent authority may extend provisional validity by periods of three months up to 12 months, and the authority or notified body assuming the functions shall immediately inform the Commission, other Member States and other notified bodies.
evidence_span: the certificates shall remain valid in one of the following circumstances

statement_summary: The Commission shall investigate cases where there are reasons to doubt a notified body competence or continued fulfilment of Article 31, may obtain relevant information from the notifying authority on request, shall treat sensitive information confidentially under Article 78, and where a notified body does not meet requirements shall inform the notifying Member State and request corrective measures including suspension or withdrawal, failing which the Commission may by implementing act suspend, restrict or withdraw the designation under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: The Commission shall, where necessary, investigate all cases where there are reasons to doubt the competence of a notified body

statement_summary: The Commission shall ensure that appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies is put in place and properly operated in the form of a sectoral group of notified bodies; each notifying authority shall ensure that the bodies notified by it participate in the group's work, directly or through designated representatives; the Commission shall provide for the exchange of knowledge and best practices between notifying authorities.
evidence_span: The Commission shall ensure that, with regard to high-risk AI systems, appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies

statement_summary: Conformity assessment bodies established under the law of a third country with which the Union has concluded an agreement may be authorised to carry out the activities of notified bodies provided they meet the Article 31 requirements or ensure an equivalent level of compliance.
evidence_span: may be authorised to carry out the activities of notified bodies under this Regulation

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models in conformity with harmonised standards published in the Official Journal in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 are presumed to be in conformity with Section 2 requirements or Chapter V Sections 2 and 3 obligations to the extent the standards cover them.
evidence_span: shall be presumed to be in conformity with the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter

statement_summary: In accordance with Article 10 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 the Commission shall without undue delay issue standardisation requests covering all Section 2 requirements and Chapter V Sections 2 and 3 obligations, asking also for deliverables on reporting and documentation processes to improve resource performance and energy-efficient development of general-purpose AI models, consult the Board and relevant stakeholders including the advisory forum, specify that standards be clear and consistent, and request European standardisation organisations to provide evidence of their best efforts.
evidence_span: the Commission shall issue, without undue delay, standardisation requests covering all requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter

statement_summary: The participants in the standardisation process shall seek to promote investment and innovation in AI, competitiveness and growth of the Union market, global cooperation on standardisation taking into account international standards, and multi-stakeholder governance with balanced representation of interests and effective participation of relevant stakeholders in accordance with Articles 5, 6 and 7 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012.
evidence_span: The participants in the standardisation process shall seek to promote investment and innovation in AI

statement_summary: The Commission may adopt implementing acts establishing common specifications for the Section 2 requirements or Chapter V Sections 2 and 3 obligations where it has requested a harmonised standard under Article 10(1) of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 and the request was not accepted, standards were not delivered in time, insufficiently address fundamental rights concerns or do not comply with the request, and no reference to harmonised standards has been or is expected to be published; it shall consult the advisory forum and adopt the acts under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: The Commission may adopt, implementing acts establishing common specifications for the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter

statement_summary: Before preparing a draft implementing act the Commission shall inform the committee referred to in Article 22 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 that it considers the conditions for common specifications to be fulfilled.
evidence_span: the Commission shall inform the committee referred to in Article 22 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models in conformity with common specifications are presumed to be in conformity with the Section 2 requirements or Chapter V Sections 2 and 3 obligations to the extent those specifications cover them.
evidence_span: shall be presumed to be in conformity with the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter

statement_summary: Where a harmonised standard is adopted by a European standardisation organisation and proposed for publication of its reference, the Commission shall assess it in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 and, when the reference is published, repeal the implementing acts or parts covering the same requirements or obligations.
evidence_span: the Commission shall assess the harmonised standard in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012
