statement_summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models that do not comply with the common specifications shall duly justify that they have adopted technical solutions meeting the requirements or obligations at a level at least equivalent.
evidence_span: they shall duly justify that they have adopted technical solutions that meet the requirements

statement_summary: A Member State that considers that a common specification does not entirely meet the requirements shall inform the Commission with a detailed explanation and the Commission shall assess the information and, if appropriate, amend the implementing act.
evidence_span: it shall inform the Commission thereof with a detailed explanation

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems trained and tested on data reflecting the specific setting of intended use are presumed to comply with Article 10(4), and systems certified under a cybersecurity scheme pursuant to Regulation (EU) 2019/881 with references published in the Official Journal are presumed to comply with the Article 15 cybersecurity requirements in so far as the certificate covers them.
evidence_span: shall be presumed to comply with the relevant requirements laid down in Article 10(4)

statement_summary: For Annex III point 1 high-risk systems where the provider has applied harmonised standards or common specifications, the provider shall opt for the conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI) or on assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation with a notified body (Annex VII); the provider shall follow the Annex VII procedure where no standards or common specifications exist, were not applied or only partly applied, or were published with restriction.
evidence_span: the provider shall opt for one of the following conformity assessment procedures based on

statement_summary: For the Annex VII procedure the provider may choose any notified body; where the system is intended to be put into service by law enforcement, immigration or asylum authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, the market surveillance authority referred to in Article 74(8) or (9) shall act as a notified body.
evidence_span: the provider may choose any of the notified bodies

statement_summary: For Annex III points 2 to 8 systems providers shall follow the internal control procedure of Annex VI; for systems covered by Annex I Section A legislation the provider shall follow the relevant conformity assessment procedure under those acts, with Section 2 requirements part of that assessment, and a manufacturer able to opt out of third-party assessment may do so only if it applied harmonised standards or common specifications covering all Section 2 requirements.
evidence_span: providers shall follow the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control as referred to in Annex VI

statement_summary: For assessments under Annex I Section A legislation, notified bodies notified under those acts are entitled to control conformity with the Section 2 requirements provided their compliance with Article 31(4), (5), (10) and (11) has been assessed in the notification procedure under those acts.
evidence_span: notified bodies which have been notified under those legal acts shall be entitled to control the conformity of the high-risk AI systems with the requirements set out in Section 2

statement_summary: High-risk AI systems already subject to a conformity assessment shall undergo a new one in the event of a substantial modification, but pre-determined changes documented in the technical documentation do not constitute a substantial modification.
evidence_span: shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend Annexes VI and VII in light of technical progress, and to amend paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 43 in order to subject Annex III points 2 to 8 systems to the Annex VII procedure or parts thereof, taking into account the effectiveness of internal control and notified body capacities.
evidence_span: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend Annexes VI and VII

statement_summary: Certificates issued by notified bodies under Annex VII shall be drawn up in a language easily understood by the relevant authorities of the Member State of establishment and be valid for the period they indicate (at most five years for Annex I systems and four years for Annex III systems), extendable at the request of the provider based on re-assessment.
evidence_span: Certificates issued by notified bodies in accordance with Annex VII shall be drawn-up in a language which can be easily understood

statement_summary: Where a notified body finds that an AI system no longer meets Section 2 requirements it shall, proportionately, suspend, withdraw or restrict the certificate unless the provider ensures compliance by corrective action within the body's deadline, and shall give reasons; an appeal procedure against decisions of notified bodies shall be available.
evidence_span: it shall, taking account of the principle of proportionality, suspend or withdraw the certificate issued or impose restrictions on it

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of certificates and approvals issued, refusals, restrictions, suspensions or withdrawals of certificates or approvals, circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of notification, requests for information from market surveillance authorities, and on request of conformity assessment activities performed.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of the following

statement_summary: Each notified body shall inform the other notified bodies of quality management system approvals and technical documentation assessment certificates it has refused, suspended, withdrawn or restricted and, on request, of those issued, and shall provide other notified bodies carrying out similar conformity assessment activities with relevant information on negative and, on request, positive conformity assessment results.
evidence_span: Each notified body shall inform the other notified bodies of

statement_summary: Notified bodies shall safeguard the confidentiality of the information that they obtain, in accordance with Article 78.
evidence_span: Notified bodies shall safeguard the confidentiality of the information that they obtain

statement_summary: By derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, any market surveillance authority may authorise for a limited period the placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems in its Member State for exceptional reasons of public security, protection of life and health, environmental protection or protection of key industrial and infrastructural assets, with conformity assessment completed without undue delay; for Annex I Section A products only derogations in that legislation apply.
evidence_span: any market surveillance authority may authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems

statement_summary: In a duly justified urgency for exceptional reasons of public security or specific, substantial and imminent threat to life or physical safety, law-enforcement or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation, provided authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay; if refused, use shall be stopped with immediate effect and all results and outputs discarded.
evidence_span: law-enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation referred to in paragraph 1

statement_summary: The authorisation shall be issued only if the market surveillance authority concludes that the high-risk AI system complies with Section 2; the authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of any authorisation issued, excluding sensitive operational data of law-enforcement authorities; an authorisation to which neither a Member State nor the Commission objects within 15 calendar days is deemed justified.
evidence_span: The market surveillance authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States of any authorisation issued

statement_summary: Where, within 15 calendar days, a Member State objects to an authorisation issued by another Member State authority or the Commission considers it contrary to Union law or its compliance conclusion unfounded, the Commission shall without delay consult the relevant Member State, consult the operators concerned and let them present their views, decide whether the authorisation is justified and address its decision to the Member State and the operators; where the Commission considers the authorisation unjustified it shall be withdrawn by the market surveillance authority.
evidence_span: the Commission shall, without delay, enter into consultations with the relevant Member State

statement_summary: The provider shall draw up a written, machine readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system, identifying the system, stating that it meets Section 2, containing the Annex V information and translated, drawn up as a single declaration where other Union legislation requires one, kept at the disposal of national competent authorities for 10 years and submitted in copy upon request, and by drawing it up assumes responsibility for compliance with Section 2 and keeps it up to date.
evidence_span: The provider shall draw up a written machine readable, physical or electronically signed EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend Annex V by updating the content of the EU declaration of conformity to introduce elements that become necessary in light of technical progress.
evidence_span: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend Annex V

statement_summary: The CE marking is subject to the general principles of Article 30 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008, shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly (or digitally and accessibly for systems provided digitally), shall be followed by the identification number of the responsible notified body affixed by the body itself or under its instructions by the provider or authorised representative and indicated in promotional material, and shall indicate conformity with other Union law that also provides for CE marking.
evidence_span: The CE marking shall be affixed visibly, legibly and indelibly for high-risk AI systems

statement_summary: Before placing on the market or putting into service a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III (except point 2) or an AI system the provider concluded is not high-risk under Article 6(3), the provider or where applicable the authorised representative shall register themselves and the system in the EU database referred to in Article 71.
evidence_span: the provider or, where applicable, the authorised representative shall register themselves and their system in the EU database referred to in Article 71

statement_summary: Before putting into service or using an Annex III high-risk AI system (except point 2), deployers that are public authorities, Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies or persons acting on their behalf shall register themselves, select the system and register its use in the EU database.
evidence_span: shall register themselves, select the system and register its use in the EU database referred to in Article 71

statement_summary: For Annex III points 1, 6 and 7 systems in law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management registration shall be in a secure non-public section of the EU database with only the listed Annex VIII and IX information and access limited to the Commission and the national authorities referred to in Article 74(8); Annex III point 2 systems shall be registered at national level; the provisions name no obligor for the restricted access rule.
evidence_span: the registration referred to in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of this Article shall be in a secure non-public section of the EU database

statement_summary: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed so that the persons concerned are informed that they are interacting with an AI system, unless obvious to a reasonably well-informed observer, with an exception for systems authorised by law to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute criminal offences.
evidence_span: Providers shall ensure that AI systems intended to interact directly with natural persons are designed and developed in such a way that the natural persons concerned are informed

statement_summary: Providers of AI systems, including general-purpose AI systems, generating synthetic audio, image, video or text content shall ensure that outputs are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated, with effective, interoperable, robust and reliable technical solutions as far as technically feasible, with stated exceptions.
evidence_span: shall ensure that the outputs of the AI system are marked in a machine-readable format and detectable as artificially generated or manipulated

statement_summary: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system and process personal data in accordance with data protection law, with an exception for systems permitted by law to detect, prevent or investigate criminal offences.
evidence_span: Deployers of an emotion recognition system or a biometric categorisation system shall inform the natural persons exposed thereto of the operation of the system

statement_summary: Deployers of an AI system generating or manipulating image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, or text published to inform the public on matters of public interest, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated, with exceptions and limited disclosure for evidently artistic, creative, satirical or fictional works, and the information shall be provided to the natural persons concerned clearly and distinguishably at the latest at first interaction or exposure and conform to accessibility requirements.
evidence_span: Deployers of an AI system that generates or manipulates image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake, shall disclose that the content has been artificially generated or manipulated

statement_summary: Article 50(1) to (4) does not affect the requirements and obligations of Chapter III and is without prejudice to other transparency obligations in Union or national law for deployers.
evidence_span: shall not affect the requirements and obligations set out in Chapter III

statement_summary: The AI Office (construed as the Commission) shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level on the detection and labelling of artificially generated or manipulated content; the Commission may approve those codes by implementing act under Article 56(6) or, if a code is not adequate, specify common rules by implementing act under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level

statement_summary: A general-purpose AI model is classified as a model with systemic risk if it has high impact capabilities (presumed when training computation exceeds 10^25 floating point operations) or, by a decision of the Commission ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel, has equivalent capabilities or impact having regard to the Annex XIII criteria.
evidence_span: A general-purpose AI model shall be classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk if it meets any of the following conditions

statement_summary: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend the thresholds in paragraphs 1 and 2 and supplement benchmarks and indicators in light of evolving technological developments when necessary for the thresholds to reflect the state of the art.
evidence_span: The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to amend the thresholds listed in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this Article

statement_summary: Where a general-purpose AI model meets the high-impact-capabilities condition the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and within two weeks after the requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met, including the information necessary to demonstrate it; if the Commission becomes aware of an un-notified model presenting systemic risks it may designate it.
evidence_span: the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks

statement_summary: The provider may present with its notification sufficiently substantiated arguments that, exceptionally, its model does not present systemic risks due to its specific characteristics; where the Commission concludes the arguments are not sufficiently substantiated it shall reject them and the model shall be considered a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk.
evidence_span: may present, with its notification, sufficiently substantiated arguments

statement_summary: The Commission may designate a general-purpose AI model as presenting systemic risks, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel pursuant to Article 90(1) point (a), on the basis of Annex XIII criteria, and may adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to amend Annex XIII.
evidence_span: The Commission may designate a general-purpose AI model as presenting systemic risks, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel

statement_summary: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated, the Commission shall take the request into account and may decide to reassess whether the model still presents systemic risks; the request must contain objective, detailed and new reasons and may be made at the earliest six months after the designation decision or after a decision maintaining the designation.
evidence_span: Upon a reasoned request of a provider whose model has been designated

statement_summary: The Commission shall ensure that a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk is published and kept up to date, without prejudice to intellectual property rights, confidential business information and trade secrets.
evidence_span: The Commission shall ensure that a list of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk is published

statement_summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall draw up and keep up to date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and evaluation results, containing at least the Annex XI information, for the purpose of providing it upon request to the AI Office and the national competent authorities.
evidence_span: draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model

statement_summary: Providers shall draw up, keep up to date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems that intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model, enabling them to understand its capabilities and limitations and comply with their obligations and containing at least the Annex XII elements, without prejudice to intellectual property rights and trade secrets.
evidence_span: draw up, keep up-to-date and make available information and documentation to providers of AI systems who intend to integrate the general-purpose AI model into their AI systems

statement_summary: Providers shall put in place a policy to comply with Union copyright law, in particular to identify and comply with a reservation of rights expressed under Article 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790, including through state-of-the-art technologies.
evidence_span: put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights

statement_summary: Providers shall draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the general-purpose AI model, according to a template provided by the AI Office.
evidence_span: draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training of the general-purpose AI model

statement_summary: The obligations in Article 53(1) points (a) and (b) do not apply to providers of models released under a free and open-source licence allowing access, usage, modification and distribution with publicly available parameters, weights, architecture and usage information, except for general-purpose AI models with systemic risks.
evidence_span: shall not apply to providers of AI models that are released under a free and open-source licence

statement_summary: Providers of general-purpose AI models shall cooperate as necessary with the Commission and the national competent authorities in the exercise of their competences and powers.
evidence_span: shall cooperate as necessary with the Commission and the national competent authorities

statement_summary: Providers may rely on codes of practice under Article 56 to demonstrate compliance with Article 53(1) until a harmonised standard is published; compliance with European harmonised standards grants the presumption of conformity to the extent they cover the obligations; providers who do not adhere to an approved code or comply with a harmonised standard shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission.
evidence_span: may rely on codes of practice within the meaning of Article 56 to demonstrate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article

statement_summary: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to detail measurement and calculation methodologies for Annex XI points 2(d) and (e) and to amend Annexes XI and XII in light of evolving technological developments.
evidence_span: the Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 to detail measurement and calculation methodologies

statement_summary: Any information or documentation obtained pursuant to Article 53, including trade secrets, shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78; no addressee position is named.
evidence_span: shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78

statement_summary: Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall by written mandate appoint an authorised representative established in the Union and enable it to perform the tasks in the mandate; the mandate shall empower the representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the AI Office or the competent authorities on all issues of compliance.
evidence_span: providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union

statement_summary: The authorised representative shall perform the tasks in the mandate, provide a copy of the mandate to the AI Office upon request, and the mandate shall empower it to verify the Annex XI technical documentation and compliance with Articles 53 and 55, keep the technical documentation and provider contact details at the disposal of the AI Office and national competent authorities for 10 years, provide information and documentation to the AI Office on reasoned request, and cooperate with the AI Office and competent authorities.
evidence_span: The authorised representative shall perform the tasks specified in the mandate received from the provider

statement_summary: The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations and shall also immediately inform the AI Office of the termination and the reasons; the Article 54 obligation does not apply to providers of open-source licence models unless they present systemic risks.
evidence_span: The authorised representative shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations

statement_summary: In addition to Articles 53 and 54, providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk shall perform model evaluation including adversarial testing, assess and mitigate possible systemic risks at Union level, keep track of, document and report without undue delay to the AI Office and as appropriate national competent authorities information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures, and ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity protection.
evidence_span: providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk shall

statement_summary: Providers of models with systemic risk may rely on codes of practice under Article 56 to demonstrate compliance with Article 55(1) until a harmonised standard is published, with the presumption of conformity for harmonised standards, and shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission where they do not adhere to an approved code or comply with a harmonised standard; information obtained is treated confidentially under Article 78.
evidence_span: may rely on codes of practice within the meaning of Article 56 to demonstrate compliance with the obligations set out in paragraph 1 of this Article

statement_summary: Any information or documentation obtained pursuant to Article 55, including trade secrets, shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78; no addressee position is named.
evidence_span: shall be treated in accordance with the confidentiality obligations set out in Article 78

statement_summary: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level to contribute to the proper application of the Regulation taking into account international approaches, and as appropriate encourage and facilitate their review and adaptation in light of emerging standards and assist in the assessment of available standards.
evidence_span: The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level

statement_summary: The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that the codes of practice cover at least the obligations in Articles 53 and 55 including the listed issues, clearly set out specific objectives, contain commitments or measures including key performance indicators as appropriate, and take due account of the needs and interests of all interested parties, including affected persons.
evidence_span: The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that the codes of practice cover at least the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55

statement_summary: The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models and relevant national competent authorities to participate in drawing up codes of practice and may invite providers to adhere to them (limited to Article 53 for models without systemic risk unless they declare interest in the full code); civil society, industry, academia and other stakeholders may support the process.
evidence_span: The AI Office may invite all providers of general-purpose AI models, as well as relevant national competent authorities, to participate in the drawing-up of codes of practice

statement_summary: The AI Office shall aim to ensure that participants to the codes of practice report regularly to the AI Office on the implementation of commitments and measures taken and their outcomes, including as measured against key performance indicators, reflecting differences in size and capacity between participants.
evidence_span: participants to the codes of practice report regularly to the AI Office on the implementation of the commitments

statement_summary: The AI Office and the Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of the objectives of the codes of practice by the participants, assess whether the codes cover the obligations in Articles 53 and 55 and publish their assessment of adequacy; the Commission may by implementing act approve a code of practice and give it general validity within the Union under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: The AI Office and the Board shall regularly monitor and evaluate the achievement of the objectives of the codes of practice by the participants

statement_summary: Codes of practice shall be ready at the latest by 2 May 2025 and the AI Office shall take the necessary steps including inviting providers; if by 2 August 2025 a code cannot be finalised or the AI Office deems it not adequate, the Commission may provide by implementing acts common rules for the obligations in Articles 53 and 55 under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: the Commission may provide, by means of implementing acts, common rules for the implementation of the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55

statement_summary: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level, operational by 2 August 2026, possibly jointly or by participating in an existing sandbox with equivalent national coverage, and additional sandboxes at regional or local level may be established; the Commission may provide technical support, advice and tools; the European Data Protection Supervisor may establish a sandbox for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies.
evidence_span: Member States shall ensure that their competent authorities establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level

statement_summary: National competent authorities shall cooperate with other relevant authorities where appropriate and may allow the involvement of other actors within the AI ecosystem; the Article does not affect other regulatory sandboxes and Member States shall ensure cooperation between the authorities supervising those sandboxes and the national competent authorities.
evidence_span: Where appropriate, national competent authorities shall cooperate with other relevant authorities

statement_summary: AI regulatory sandboxes shall provide a controlled environment fostering innovation and facilitating development, training, testing and validation of innovative AI systems for a limited time before placing on the market or putting into service pursuant to a specific sandbox plan agreed between providers or prospective providers and the competent authority, may include supervised testing in real world conditions, aim at stated objectives and facilitate cross-border cooperation.
evidence_span: pursuant to a specific sandbox plan agreed between the providers or prospective providers and the competent authority

statement_summary: Competent authorities shall provide, as appropriate, guidance, supervision and support within the AI regulatory sandbox to identify risks, test and mitigate and shall provide providers and prospective providers participating in the sandbox with guidance on regulatory expectations and how to fulfil the requirements and obligations.
evidence_span: Competent authorities shall provide providers and prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox with guidance on regulatory expectations

statement_summary: Upon request of the provider or prospective provider the competent authority shall provide written proof of the activities successfully carried out in the sandbox and an exit report; market surveillance authorities and notified bodies shall take the exit reports and written proof provided by the national competent authority positively into account to accelerate conformity assessment procedures to a reasonable extent.
evidence_span: Upon request of the provider or prospective provider of the AI system, the competent authority shall provide a written proof of the activities successfully carried out in the sandbox

statement_summary: Subject to Article 78 and with the agreement of the provider or prospective provider, the Commission and the Board are authorised to access the exit reports and take them into account when exercising their tasks; if both the provider and the national competent authority explicitly agree the exit report may be made publicly available through the single information platform.
evidence_span: the Commission and the Board shall be authorised to access the exit reports

statement_summary: National competent authorities shall ensure that, where innovative AI systems involve personal data or fall under the supervisory remit of other national or competent authorities, the national data protection authorities and those other authorities are associated with the operation of the sandbox and involved in supervision to the extent of their tasks and powers.
evidence_span: the national data protection authorities and those other national or competent authorities are associated with the operation of the AI regulatory sandbox

statement_summary: Sandboxes do not affect the supervisory or corrective powers of the competent authorities; significant risks identified shall result in adequate mitigation; national competent authorities have the power to temporarily or permanently suspend the testing process or participation if no effective mitigation is possible and shall inform the AI Office of the decision, exercising supervisory powers within the limits of the relevant law using discretion to support innovation.
evidence_span: National competent authorities shall have the power to temporarily or permanently suspend the testing process, or the participation in the sandbox

statement_summary: Providers and prospective providers participating in the sandbox remain liable under applicable Union and national liability law for damage inflicted on third parties; provided they observe the sandbox plan and terms and follow in good faith the guidance of the national competent authority, no administrative fines shall be imposed for infringements of the Regulation, and no fines under other law where other competent authorities were actively involved and provided guidance.
evidence_span: no administrative fines shall be imposed by the authorities for infringements of this Regulation

statement_summary: National competent authorities shall coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board.
evidence_span: National competent authorities shall coordinate their activities and cooperate within the framework of the Board

statement_summary: National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox and may ask them for support and guidance; the AI Office shall make publicly available and keep up to date a list of planned and existing sandboxes.
evidence_span: National competent authorities shall inform the AI Office and the Board of the establishment of a sandbox

statement_summary: National competent authorities shall submit annual reports and a final report to the AI Office and the Board on the progress and results of sandboxes, including best practices, incidents, lessons learnt and recommendations, shall make the reports or abstracts available to the public online, and the Commission shall where appropriate take them into account.
evidence_span: National competent authorities shall submit annual reports to the AI Office and to the Board

statement_summary: The Commission shall develop a single and dedicated interface containing relevant information on AI regulatory sandboxes to allow stakeholders to interact with sandboxes, raise enquiries with competent authorities and seek non-binding guidance on conformity, and shall proactively coordinate with national competent authorities where relevant.
evidence_span: The Commission shall develop a single and dedicated interface containing all relevant information related to AI regulatory sandboxes

statement_summary: To avoid fragmentation the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation and supervision of AI regulatory sandboxes, including common principles on eligibility and selection criteria, procedures for application, participation, monitoring, exit and termination including the sandbox plan and exit report, and terms and conditions for participants, under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation and supervision of the AI regulatory sandboxes

statement_summary: The implementing acts shall ensure that sandboxes are open to any applying provider or prospective provider meeting transparent and fair criteria, with decisions communicated within three months, broad and equal access, flexibility for national competent authorities, free access for SMEs, facilitation of conformity assessment and codes of conduct, involvement of other ecosystem actors, simple and streamlined procedures with mutual and uniform recognition of participation across the Union, a participation period appropriate to the project, and tools and infrastructure for testing and benchmarking; the content concerns the future implementing acts, which are outside W.
evidence_span: The implementing acts referred to in paragraph 1 shall ensure

statement_summary: Prospective providers in the sandboxes, in particular SMEs and start-ups, shall be directed where relevant to pre-deployment services such as guidance, help with standardisation documents and certification, testing and experimentation facilities, European Digital Innovation Hubs and centres of excellence; no obligor is named.
evidence_span: shall be directed, where relevant, to pre-deployment services

statement_summary: Where national competent authorities consider authorising supervised testing in real world conditions within a sandbox they shall specifically agree the terms and conditions and the appropriate safeguards with the participants to protect fundamental rights, health and safety and, where appropriate, cooperate with other national competent authorities to ensure consistent practices across the Union.
evidence_span: they shall specifically agree the terms and conditions of such testing and, in particular, the appropriate safeguards with the participants

statement_summary: In the sandbox personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed solely for developing, training and testing certain AI systems when all cumulative conditions are met: development for substantial public interest in listed areas, necessity for Section 2 requirements, effective monitoring and response mechanisms, a functionally separate protected processing environment under the control of the prospective provider, restricted sharing, no measures or decisions affecting data subjects, protection and deletion, logging, documentation as part of technical documentation, and publication of a project summary on the competent authority websites.
evidence_span: personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed solely for the purpose of developing, training and testing certain AI systems in the sandbox

statement_summary: For criminal-justice purposes under the control and responsibility of law enforcement authorities, processing of personal data in sandboxes shall be based on a specific Union or national law and subject to the same cumulative conditions as in paragraph 1.
evidence_span: the processing of personal data in AI regulatory sandboxes shall be based on a specific Union or national law and subject to the same cumulative conditions

statement_summary: Article 59(1) is without prejudice to Union or national law which excludes processing of personal data for other purposes, or lays down the basis for processing necessary for developing, testing or training innovative AI systems or any other legal basis, in compliance with Union data protection law.
evidence_span: Paragraph 1 is without prejudice to Union or national law which excludes processing of personal data for other purposes

statement_summary: Providers or prospective providers of Annex III high-risk AI systems may conduct testing in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes, at any time before placing on the market or putting into service, on their own or in partnership with deployers, in accordance with Article 60 and the real-world testing plan, without prejudice to Article 5, ethical review and Union or national law on testing of Annex I products.
evidence_span: may be conducted by providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III

statement_summary: The Commission shall, by implementing acts under the examination procedure of Article 98(2), specify the detailed elements of the real-world testing plan.
evidence_span: The Commission shall, by means of implementing acts, specify the detailed elements of the real-world testing plan

statement_summary: Testing in real world conditions may be conducted only where, among other conditions, the provider has drawn up and submitted a real-world testing plan to the market surveillance authority and the authority has approved it (tacitly after 30 days, unless national law requires authorisation), the testing is registered, the provider is established in the Union or has a legal representative, data transfers to third countries are safeguarded, duration is limited to six months extendable by six months on prior notification, vulnerable subjects are protected, deployers are informed and an agreement on roles is concluded, subjects give informed consent, the testing is effectively overseen and outputs can be reversed.
evidence_span: Providers or prospective providers may conduct the testing in real world conditions only where all of the following conditions are met

statement_summary: Subjects of testing in real world conditions, or their legally designated representative, may without detriment and without justification withdraw at any time by revoking their informed consent and may request immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data; withdrawal does not affect activities already carried out.
evidence_span: may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time by revoking their informed consent

statement_summary: In accordance with Article 75, Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities the powers of requiring providers and prospective providers to provide information, of carrying out unannounced remote or on-site inspections and of performing checks on the conduct of testing in real world conditions and the related systems, and the authorities shall use those powers to ensure the safe development of testing.
evidence_span: Member States shall confer on their market surveillance authorities the powers of requiring providers and prospective providers to provide information

statement_summary: Any serious incident identified in the course of testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority under Article 73, the provider or prospective provider shall adopt immediate mitigation or suspend or terminate the testing and establish a procedure for prompt recall, shall notify the authority of suspension or termination and the final outcomes, and is liable under applicable Union and national liability law for damage caused in the testing.
evidence_span: Any serious incident identified in the course of the testing in real world conditions shall be reported to the national market surveillance authority in accordance with Article 73

statement_summary: For testing under Article 60, freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects prior to participation after being informed of the nature and objectives, conditions and duration, rights including refusal and withdrawal, arrangements for reversal of outputs, the Union-wide identification number and provider contact details; the consent shall be dated and documented and a copy given to the subjects or their legal representative.
evidence_span: freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing

statement_summary: Member States shall provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or branch in the Union with priority access to the sandboxes, organise awareness raising and training tailored to SMEs, deployers and as appropriate local public authorities, utilise or establish channels for communication and advice with SMEs, deployers, other innovators and as appropriate local public authorities, and facilitate the participation of SMEs and other stakeholders in standardisation.
evidence_span: Member States shall undertake the following actions

statement_summary: The specific interests and needs of SME providers, including start-ups, shall be taken into account when setting the fees for conformity assessment under Article 43, reducing those fees proportionately to size, market size and other relevant indicators; the party setting the fees is not named.
evidence_span: shall be taken into account when setting the fees for conformity assessment under Article 43

statement_summary: The AI Office (construed as the Commission) shall provide standardised templates as specified by the Board in its request, develop and maintain a single information platform for all operators across the Union, organise communication campaigns to raise awareness and evaluate and promote the convergence of best practices in public procurement of AI systems.
evidence_span: provide standardised templates for areas covered by this Regulation, as specified by the Board in its request

statement_summary: Microenterprises without partner or linked enterprises may comply with certain elements of the Article 17 quality management system in a simplified manner and the Commission shall develop guidelines on those elements considering the needs of microenterprises, without exempting them from other requirements or obligations including Articles 9 to 15, 72 and 73.
evidence_span: may comply with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17 of this Regulation in a simplified manner

statement_summary: The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office, and Member States shall facilitate the tasks entrusted to the AI Office as reflected in the Regulation.
evidence_span: The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office

statement_summary: A European Artificial Intelligence Board is hereby established.
evidence_span: A European Artificial Intelligence Board (the ‘Board’) is hereby established

statement_summary: The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State, the European Data Protection Supervisor participating as observer and the AI Office attending meetings without voting; other national and Union authorities, bodies or experts may be invited case by case; each representative is designated by the Member State for three years, renewable once.
evidence_span: The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State

statement_summary: Member States shall ensure that their representatives on the Board have the relevant competences and powers to contribute actively to the Board tasks, are designated as a single contact point vis-a-vis the Board and where appropriate for stakeholders, and are empowered to facilitate consistency and coordination between national competent authorities in their Member State including through collection of relevant data and information.
evidence_span: Member States shall ensure that their representatives on the Board

statement_summary: The designated representatives of the Member States shall adopt the rules of procedure of the Board by a two-thirds majority; the Board shall be organised and operated so as to safeguard objectivity and impartiality; the Board is chaired by one of the Member State representatives and the AI Office provides the secretariat, convenes meetings upon request of the Chair and prepares the agenda.
evidence_span: The designated representatives of the Member States shall adopt the Board’s rules of procedure by a two-thirds majority

statement_summary: The Board shall establish two standing sub-groups to provide a platform for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities about market surveillance and notified bodies respectively, the market surveillance sub-group acting as the administrative cooperation group within the meaning of Article 30 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020; the Board may establish other sub-groups and invite representatives of the advisory forum as observers.
evidence_span: The Board shall establish two standing sub-groups to provide a platform for cooperation and exchange among market surveillance authorities and notifying authorities

statement_summary: The Board shall advise and assist the Commission and the Member States to facilitate consistent and effective application, and may in particular contribute to coordination among national competent authorities and support joint market surveillance activities, share expertise and best practices, advise on implementation including enforcement on general-purpose AI models, contribute to harmonising administrative practices, issue recommendations and written opinions at the request of the Commission or on its own initiative, support AI literacy, facilitate common criteria, cooperate with other Union bodies and with third countries, assist national competent authorities and the Commission in developing expertise, assist the AI Office in supporting sandboxes, advise on guidance and international matters, provide opinions to the Commission on qualified alerts regarding general-purpose AI models and receive opinions of Member States on such alerts.
evidence_span: The Board shall advise and assist the Commission and the Member States in order to facilitate the consistent and effective application of this Regulation

statement_summary: An advisory forum shall be established to provide technical expertise and advise the Board and the Commission and contribute to their tasks.
evidence_span: An advisory forum shall be established to provide technical expertise and advise the Board and the Commission

statement_summary: The membership of the advisory forum shall represent a balanced selection of stakeholders, including industry, start-ups, SMEs, civil society and academia, balanced between commercial and non-commercial interests and between SMEs and other undertakings; the Commission shall appoint the members from stakeholders with recognised expertise in AI; the term of office is two years, extendable by up to four years.
evidence_span: The Commission shall appoint the members of the advisory forum

statement_summary: The Fundamental Rights Agency, ENISA, CEN, CENELEC and ETSI shall be permanent members of the advisory forum.
evidence_span: shall be permanent members of the advisory forum

statement_summary: The advisory forum shall draw up its rules of procedure, elect two co-chairs, hold meetings at least twice a year, may invite experts and other stakeholders and establish sub-groups, and shall prepare an annual report on its activities which shall be made publicly available.
evidence_span: The advisory forum shall draw up its rules of procedure

statement_summary: The advisory forum may prepare opinions, recommendations and written contributions at the request of the Board or the Commission.
evidence_span: The advisory forum may prepare opinions, recommendations and written contributions at the request of the Board or the Commission

statement_summary: The Commission shall, by an implementing act under the examination procedure of Article 98(2), make provisions on the establishment of a scientific panel of independent experts intended to support enforcement activities, including conditions, procedures and detailed arrangements for the panel and its members to issue alerts and to request the assistance of the AI Office.
evidence_span: The Commission shall, by means of an implementing act, make provisions on the establishment of a scientific panel of independent experts

statement_summary: The scientific panel shall consist of experts selected by the Commission on the basis of up-to-date scientific or technical expertise in AI who demonstrate particular expertise, independence from any provider of AI systems or general-purpose AI models and ability to carry out activities diligently, accurately and objectively; the Commission, in consultation with the Board, shall determine the number of experts and ensure fair gender and geographical representation.
evidence_span: The scientific panel shall consist of experts selected by the Commission

statement_summary: The scientific panel shall advise and support the AI Office on the implementation and enforcement of the Regulation as regards general-purpose AI models and systems, including alerting the AI Office of possible systemic risks under Article 90, contributing to tools and methodologies, advising on classification, supporting the work of market surveillance authorities at their request and cross-border market surveillance activities, and supporting the AI Office in the Union safeguard procedure under Article 81.
evidence_span: The scientific panel shall advise and support the AI Office

statement_summary: The experts of the scientific panel shall perform tasks with impartiality and objectivity, ensure confidentiality, neither seek nor take instructions, and each draw up a publicly available declaration of interests; the AI Office shall establish systems and procedures to manage and prevent conflicts of interest.
evidence_span: The experts on the scientific panel shall perform their tasks with impartiality and objectivity

statement_summary: Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities, may be required to pay fees set out in the Article 68(1) implementing act, and the Commission shall facilitate timely access to the experts and ensure that the support of Union AI testing support under Article 84 and of the experts is efficiently organised.
evidence_span: Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities under this Regulation

statement_summary: Each Member State shall establish or designate as national competent authorities at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority, which shall exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias, with members refraining from incompatible action, and such tasks may be performed by one or more designated authorities.
evidence_span: Each Member State shall establish or designate as national competent authorities at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority

statement_summary: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the identity and tasks of the notifying and market surveillance authorities and any changes, make publicly available by 2 August 2025 information on how competent authorities and single points of contact can be contacted, designate a market surveillance authority as the single point of contact and notify its identity to the Commission, and the Commission shall make the list of single points of contact publicly available.
evidence_span: Member States shall communicate to the Commission the identity of the notifying authorities and the market surveillance authorities

statement_summary: Member States shall ensure that national competent authorities have adequate technical, financial and human resources and infrastructure and sufficient permanent personnel with specified competences, and shall assess and update the requirements annually; national competent authorities shall take appropriate measures to ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity and act in accordance with the confidentiality obligations of Article 78.
evidence_span: Member States shall ensure that their national competent authorities are provided with adequate technical, financial and human resources

statement_summary: By 2 August 2025 and every two years thereafter Member States shall report to the Commission on the financial and human resources of national competent authorities with an assessment of adequacy; the Commission shall transmit the information to the Board for discussion and possible recommendations and shall facilitate the exchange of experience between national competent authorities.
evidence_span: Member States shall report to the Commission on the status of the financial and human resources of the national competent authorities

statement_summary: National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on the implementation of the Regulation, in particular to SMEs including start-ups, taking into account the guidance and advice of the Board and the Commission, and shall consult the national competent authorities under other Union law whenever they intend to provide guidance on an AI system in areas covered by that law.
evidence_span: National competent authorities may provide guidance and advice on the implementation of this Regulation, in particular to SMEs including start-ups

statement_summary: Where Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies fall within the scope of the Regulation, the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as the competent authority for their supervision.
evidence_span: the European Data Protection Supervisor shall act as the competent authority for their supervision

statement_summary: The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database containing the information of paragraphs 2 and 3 on high-risk AI systems and on AI systems not considered high-risk under Article 6(3), registered under Articles 6(4), 49 and 60; it shall consult relevant experts when setting the functional specifications and the Board when updating them.
evidence_span: The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database

statement_summary: The data listed in Sections A and B of Annex VIII shall be entered into the EU database by the provider or where applicable the authorised representative, and the data in Section C of Annex VIII by the deployer who is or acts on behalf of a public authority, agency or body, in accordance with Article 49(3) and (4).
evidence_span: shall be entered into the EU database by the provider or, where applicable, by the authorised representative

statement_summary: With the exception of the restricted sections, the information in the EU database registered under Article 49 shall be accessible and publicly available in a user-friendly, navigable and machine-readable manner; information registered under Article 60 is accessible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission unless the provider consents to public access; the database shall contain personal data only in so far as necessary, including names and contact details of natural persons responsible for registration.
evidence_span: shall be accessible only to market surveillance authorities and the Commission

statement_summary: The Commission shall be the controller of the EU database, shall make available to providers, prospective providers and deployers adequate technical and administrative support, and the database shall comply with applicable accessibility requirements.
evidence_span: The Commission shall be the controller of the EU database

statement_summary: Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks, which shall actively and systematically collect, document and analyse relevant data (which may be provided by deployers or collected through other sources) on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime to evaluate continuous compliance with Section 2, shall be based on a post-market monitoring plan forming part of the technical documentation, and shall not cover sensitive operational data of law-enforcement deployers.
evidence_span: Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system

statement_summary: The Commission shall adopt an implementing act laying down detailed provisions establishing a template for the post-market monitoring plan and the list of elements to be included by 2 February 2026, under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: The Commission shall adopt an implementing act laying down detailed provisions establishing a template for the post-market monitoring plan

statement_summary: For high-risk AI systems covered by Annex I Section A legislation where a post-market monitoring system and plan already exist under that legislation, providers may integrate the necessary elements of Article 72(1) to (3) into existing systems and plans provided an equivalent level of protection is achieved, and this also applies to Annex III point 5 systems placed on the market or put into service by financial institutions subject to Union financial services law internal governance requirements.
evidence_span: providers shall have a choice of integrating, as appropriate, the necessary elements described in paragraphs 1, 2 and 3

statement_summary: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member State where it occurred, immediately after establishing a causal link or its reasonable likelihood and in any event within 15 days (two days for widespread infringements or critical-infrastructure incidents, ten days for death), taking account of severity and possibly by an initial incomplete report.
evidence_span: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities

statement_summary: Following the report the provider shall without delay perform the necessary investigations including a risk assessment and corrective action, cooperate with the competent authorities and where relevant the notified body, and shall not perform an investigation altering the AI system in a way that may affect evaluation of the causes prior to informing the competent authorities.
evidence_span: the provider shall, without delay, perform the necessary investigations in relation to the serious incident and the AI system concerned

statement_summary: Upon receiving a notification of a serious incident referred to in Article 3 point (49)(c) (infringement of fundamental-rights obligations) the market surveillance authority shall inform the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1), and the Commission shall develop dedicated guidance on the reporting obligations by 2 August 2025 and assess it regularly.
evidence_span: the relevant market surveillance authority shall inform the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1)

statement_summary: The market surveillance authority shall take appropriate measures as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 within seven days from receipt of the notification and follow the notification procedures of that Regulation, and national competent authorities shall immediately notify the Commission of any serious incident in accordance with Article 20 of that Regulation.
evidence_span: shall take appropriate measures, as provided for in Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, within seven days

statement_summary: For Annex III high-risk AI systems placed by providers subject to equivalent reporting obligations under other Union legislative instruments, notification of serious incidents is limited to those under Article 3 point (49)(c); for systems that are safety components of or are devices covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and (EU) 2017/746 the same limitation applies and the notification is made to the national competent authority chosen by the Member States where the incident occurred.
evidence_span: the notification of serious incidents shall be limited to those referred to in Article 3, point (49)(c)

statement_summary: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies to AI systems covered by the Regulation, references to an economic operator including all operators identified in Article 2(1) and references to a product including all AI systems; Articles 79 to 83 do not apply to AI systems related to Annex I Section A products where sectoral legislation provides equivalent procedures.
evidence_span: Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply to AI systems covered by this Regulation

statement_summary: As part of their reporting obligations under Article 34(4) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 market surveillance authorities shall report annually to the Commission and relevant national competition authorities information identified in market surveillance that may be of interest for competition rules, and shall report annually to the Commission on the use of prohibited practices and the measures taken.
evidence_span: the market surveillance authorities shall report annually to the Commission and relevant national competition authorities

statement_summary: For high-risk AI systems related to Annex I Section A products the market surveillance authority is the authority designated under those acts (Member States may designate another authority ensuring coordination); for financial institutions it is the national financial supervisory authority (another authority may be identified with coordination); for Annex III point 1 law enforcement, border management and justice and democracy systems and points 6, 7 and 8 Member States shall designate the competent data protection supervisory authorities or authorities designated under Articles 41 to 44 of Directive (EU) 2016/680, without affecting the independence of judicial authorities; for Union institutions the European Data Protection Supervisor acts as market surveillance authority except for the Court of Justice acting in its judicial capacity.
evidence_span: the market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation shall be the authority responsible for market surveillance activities designated under those legal acts

statement_summary: Without prejudice to Article 14 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, market surveillance authorities may exercise the powers in Article 14(4) points (d) and (j) of that Regulation remotely, as appropriate.
evidence_span: market surveillance authorities may exercise the powers referred to in Article 14(4), points (d) and (j), of that Regulation remotely

statement_summary: Member States shall facilitate coordination between market surveillance authorities designated under the Regulation and other relevant national authorities or bodies which supervise the application of Annex I harmonisation legislation or other Union law relevant to Annex III systems.
evidence_span: Member States shall facilitate coordination between market surveillance authorities designated under this Regulation

statement_summary: Market surveillance authorities and the Commission shall be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations, to be conducted by market surveillance authorities or jointly with the Commission, to promote compliance, identify non-compliance, raise awareness or provide guidance for categories of high-risk AI systems found to present a serious risk across two or more Member States under Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, and the AI Office shall provide coordination support for joint investigations.
evidence_span: Market surveillance authorities and the Commission shall be able to propose joint activities, including joint investigations

statement_summary: Market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers, where relevant and limited to what is necessary, to documentation and the training, validation and testing data sets used for the development of high-risk AI systems, including through APIs or other remote access, and access to source code upon reasoned request only when necessary to assess conformity with Section 2 and when testing, auditing and verification based on provider data and documentation are exhausted or insufficient; information obtained is treated in accordance with Article 78.
evidence_span: the market surveillance authorities shall be granted full access by providers to the documentation as well as the training, validation and testing data sets

statement_summary: Where an AI system is based on a general-purpose AI model and both are developed by the same provider, the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of the system with obligations under the Regulation, with all the powers of a market surveillance authority under Section 3 and Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
evidence_span: the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system with obligations under this Regulation

statement_summary: Where market surveillance authorities have sufficient reason to consider that general-purpose AI systems usable directly by deployers for at least one high-risk purpose are non-compliant, they shall cooperate with the AI Office to carry out compliance evaluations and shall inform the Board and other market surveillance authorities.
evidence_span: they shall cooperate with the AI Office to carry out compliance evaluations

statement_summary: Where a market surveillance authority cannot conclude its investigation because of inability to access information related to the general-purpose AI model despite appropriate efforts, it may submit a reasoned request to the AI Office, by which access shall be enforced, and the AI Office shall supply any relevant information to the applicant authority without delay and within 30 days; market surveillance authorities safeguard confidentiality under Article 78 and Chapter VI of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies mutatis mutandis.
evidence_span: it may submit a reasoned request to the AI Office, by which access to that information shall be enforced

statement_summary: Market surveillance authorities shall have competences and powers to ensure that testing in real world conditions is in accordance with the Regulation and, for testing within a sandbox under Article 58, shall verify compliance with Article 60 as part of their supervisory role and may allow testing in derogation from Article 60(4) points (f) and (g).
evidence_span: Market surveillance authorities shall have competences and powers to ensure that testing in real world conditions is in accordance with this Regulation

statement_summary: Where a market surveillance authority has been informed of a serious incident by the prospective provider, the provider or any third party or has other grounds for considering that the conditions of Articles 60 and 61 are not met it may on its territory suspend or terminate the testing or require the provider and deployer to modify any aspect; the decision or an objection under Article 60(4)(b) shall indicate the grounds and how the provider can challenge it, and the grounds shall be communicated to the market surveillance authorities of other Member States where the system was tested.
evidence_span: it may take either of the following decisions on its territory, as appropriate

statement_summary: National public authorities or bodies which supervise or enforce the respect of obligations under Union law protecting fundamental rights in relation to the use of Annex III high-risk AI systems shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under the Regulation when necessary for fulfilling their mandates within the limits of their jurisdiction, and shall inform the market surveillance authority of the Member State concerned of any such request.
evidence_span: shall have the power to request and access any documentation created or maintained under this Regulation

statement_summary: By 2 November 2024 each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) and make a list publicly available, notify the list to the Commission and the other Member States and keep it up to date.
evidence_span: each Member State shall identify the public authorities or bodies referred to in paragraph 1 and make a list of them publicly available

statement_summary: Where the documentation is insufficient to ascertain whether an infringement of fundamental-rights obligations has occurred, the national authority or body may make a reasoned request to the market surveillance authority to organise testing of the high-risk AI system through technical means, which the authority shall organise with the close involvement of the requesting body within a reasonable time; information obtained is treated in accordance with Article 78.
evidence_span: may make a reasoned request to the market surveillance authority, to organise testing of the high-risk AI system through technical means

statement_summary: The Commission, market surveillance authorities, notified bodies and any other natural or legal person involved in the application of the Regulation shall, in accordance with Union or national law, respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained so as to protect intellectual property rights, trade secrets, effective implementation of the Regulation, public and national security interests, criminal or administrative proceedings and classified information; the authorities shall request only data strictly necessary, put in place cybersecurity measures and delete data when no longer needed.
evidence_span: shall, in accordance with Union or national law, respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities

statement_summary: Information exchanged on a confidential basis between national competent authorities or with the Commission shall not be disclosed without prior consultation of the originating national competent authority and the deployer where law enforcement, border control, immigration or asylum use of Annex III points 1, 6 or 7 systems would be jeopardised, and the exchange does not cover sensitive operational data; where such authorities are providers the Annex IV technical documentation remains on their premises, with immediate access on request by the market surveillance authorities referred to in Article 74(8) and (9), limited to staff with appropriate security clearance.
evidence_span: information exchanged on a confidential basis between the national competent authorities or between national competent authorities and the Commission shall not be disclosed

statement_summary: Article 78(1) to (3) does not affect the rights or obligations of the Commission, Member States, their authorities and notified bodies on exchange of information and dissemination of warnings or the obligations to provide information under criminal law, and the Commission and Member States may exchange confidential information with regulatory authorities of third countries with which they have concluded confidentiality arrangements guaranteeing an adequate level of confidentiality.
evidence_span: The Commission and Member States may exchange, where necessary and in accordance with relevant provisions of international and trade agreements, confidential information with regulatory authorities of third countries

statement_summary: AI systems presenting a risk to the health or safety or to fundamental rights of persons are understood as a product presenting a risk as defined in Article 3 point 19 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020.
evidence_span: AI systems presenting a risk shall be understood as a

statement_summary: Where the market surveillance authority of a Member State has sufficient reason to consider an AI system to present a risk it shall evaluate its compliance with all requirements and obligations, give particular attention to vulnerable groups, inform and cooperate with the national public authorities or bodies of Article 77(1) where fundamental-rights risks are identified, and where it finds non-compliance shall without undue delay require the relevant operator to take all appropriate corrective actions, withdraw or recall the system within a prescribed period (at most 15 working days unless sectoral legislation provides otherwise) and inform the relevant notified body; the relevant operators shall cooperate.
evidence_span: it shall carry out an evaluation of the AI system concerned in respect of its compliance with all the requirements and obligations laid down in this Regulation

statement_summary: Where non-compliance is not restricted to the national territory the market surveillance authority shall inform the Commission and the other Member States without undue delay of the results and required actions; where the operator does not take adequate corrective action the authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict making available or putting into service, withdraw or recall, and notify the Commission and the other Member States with all available details and an indication of the type of non-compliance; other market surveillance authorities inform the Commission and Member States of measures adopted and any objections.
evidence_span: it shall inform the Commission and the other Member States without undue delay of the results of the evaluation

statement_summary: The operator shall ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems it has made available on the Union market, and where it does not take adequate corrective action within the prescribed period the market surveillance authority shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict, withdraw or recall.
evidence_span: The operator shall ensure that all appropriate corrective action is taken in respect of all the AI systems concerned

statement_summary: A provisional measure taken by a market surveillance authority is deemed justified if within three months (30 days for non-compliance with the Article 5 prohibitions) no objection is raised by a market surveillance authority of another Member State or the Commission, without prejudice to the procedural rights of the operator under Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, and market surveillance authorities shall ensure that appropriate restrictive measures are taken without undue delay.
evidence_span: that measure shall be deemed justified
