statement_summary: Where a market surveillance authority has sufficient reason to consider that an AI system classified by the provider as non-high-risk under Article 6(3) is high-risk it shall evaluate it and, if it finds it high-risk, require the provider to take all necessary actions and corrective action within a prescribed period, inform the Commission and other Member States where use is not restricted to its territory; the provider shall ensure the actions and is subject to fines in accordance with Article 99 if it does not comply or misclassified to circumvent Section 2; Article 79(5) to (9) apply if corrective action is inadequate; authorities may perform checks taking into account the EU database.
evidence_span: the market surveillance authority shall carry out an evaluation of the AI system concerned in respect of its classification as a high-risk AI system

statement_summary: Where within three months (30 days for Article 5 prohibitions) of the Article 79(5) notification objections are raised by a market surveillance authority of a Member State to a measure of another authority or the Commission considers the measure contrary to Union law, the Commission shall without undue delay consult the market surveillance authority of the relevant Member State and the operator or operators, evaluate the national measure and, within six months (60 days for Article 5 prohibitions), decide whether it is justified, notify the decision to the authority concerned and inform all other market surveillance authorities; where the measure is justified all Member States shall take restrictive measures and inform the Commission, where unjustified the Member State concerned shall withdraw it; where the non-compliance is attributed to shortcomings in harmonised standards or common specifications the Commission shall apply Article 11 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012.
evidence_span: the Commission shall without undue delay enter into consultation with the market surveillance authority of the relevant Member State and the operator or operators

statement_summary: Where, after consulting the relevant national public authority of Article 77(1), a market surveillance authority finds that a compliant high-risk AI system nevertheless presents a risk to health, safety, fundamental rights or other aspects of public interest protection it shall require the relevant operator to take measures within a prescribed period, the operator shall ensure corrective action, the Member State shall immediately inform the Commission and other Member States, and the Commission shall consult the Member States concerned and the operators, evaluate the national measures, decide whether the measure is justified, propose other measures where necessary and communicate its decision to the Member States concerned and the operators and inform the other Member States.
evidence_span: it shall require the relevant operator to take all appropriate measures to ensure that the AI system concerned

statement_summary: Where a market surveillance authority finds that the CE marking was affixed in violation of Article 48 or not affixed, the EU declaration of conformity was not drawn up or not correctly, the registration in the EU database was not carried out, no authorised representative was appointed or technical documentation is unavailable, it shall require the provider to put an end to the non-compliance within a prescribed period, and where it persists shall take appropriate and proportionate measures to restrict or prohibit the system being made available or ensure it is recalled or withdrawn.
evidence_span: it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned, within a period it may prescribe

statement_summary: The Commission shall designate one or more Union AI testing support structures to perform the tasks under Article 21(6) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 in the area of AI, which shall also provide independent technical or scientific advice at the request of the Board, the Commission or market surveillance authorities.
evidence_span: The Commission shall designate one or more Union AI testing support structures

statement_summary: Without prejudice to other administrative or judicial remedies, any natural or legal person having grounds to consider that there has been an infringement of the Regulation may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority, and in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 such complaints shall be taken into account for market surveillance activities and handled in line with the dedicated procedures established by the market surveillance authorities.
evidence_span: may submit complaints to the relevant market surveillance authority

statement_summary: Any affected person subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of the output of an Annex III high-risk AI system (except point 2) which produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects that person in a way they consider adverse to health, safety or fundamental rights has the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken, subject to exceptions under Union or national law and applying only where the right is not otherwise provided under Union law.
evidence_span: shall have the right to obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken

statement_summary: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 applies to the reporting of infringements of the Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.
evidence_span: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation

statement_summary: The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94, and shall entrust the implementation to the AI Office; the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor effective implementation and compliance by providers of general-purpose AI models including adherence to approved codes of practice; market surveillance authorities may request the Commission to exercise these powers where necessary and proportionate.
evidence_span: The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V

statement_summary: Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of the Regulation, duly reasoned and indicating at least the point of contact of the provider of the general-purpose AI model, a description of the relevant facts, the provisions concerned and the reasons, and any other relevant information.
evidence_span: Downstream providers shall have the right to lodge a complaint alleging an infringement of this Regulation

statement_summary: The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect that a general-purpose AI model poses a concrete identifiable risk at Union level or meets the conditions of Article 51, duly reasoned with at least the point of contact of the provider, the facts and reasons and other relevant information; upon such alert the Commission, through the AI Office and after having informed the Board, may exercise the powers of Section 5 to assess the matter and the AI Office shall inform the Board of any measure under Articles 91 to 94.
evidence_span: The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect that

statement_summary: The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model to provide the documentation drawn up under Articles 53 and 55 or any additional information necessary to assess compliance, the AI Office may initiate a structured dialogue before the request, the Commission may issue a request upon a duly substantiated request of the scientific panel where necessary and proportionate, the request shall state the legal basis, purpose, information required, period and the fines of Article 101 for incorrect, incomplete or misleading information, and the provider or its representative shall supply the information requested.
evidence_span: The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned to provide the documentation drawn up by the provider in accordance with Articles 53 and 55

statement_summary: The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model to assess compliance where information gathered is insufficient or to investigate systemic risks in particular following a qualified alert; the Commission may appoint independent experts including from the scientific panel, may request access to the model through APIs or further technical means including source code with a statement of legal basis, purpose, period and the fines of Article 101, the provider or its representative shall provide the access requested, the AI Office may initiate a structured dialogue before requesting access, and the Commission shall adopt implementing acts on detailed arrangements for the evaluations including the involvement and selection of independent experts.
evidence_span: The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned

statement_summary: Where necessary and appropriate the Commission may request providers to take appropriate measures to comply with Articles 53 and 54, implement mitigation measures where the evaluation under Article 92 has given rise to serious and substantiated concern of a systemic risk, or restrict, withdraw or recall the model; before a measure is requested the AI Office may initiate a structured dialogue, and if the provider of a model with systemic risk offers commitments to mitigate the systemic risk the Commission may by decision make those commitments binding and declare that there are no further grounds for action.
evidence_span: the Commission may request providers to

statement_summary: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 applies mutatis mutandis to providers of general-purpose AI models, without prejudice to more specific procedural rights provided for in the Regulation.
evidence_span: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model

statement_summary: The AI Office and the Member States shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct fostering voluntary application to AI systems other than high-risk systems of some or all of the Section 2 requirements and of specific requirements to all AI systems on the basis of clear objectives and key performance indicators, taking into account the interests of SMEs; codes of conduct may be drawn up by individual providers or deployers or organisations representing them or both, including with interested stakeholders, and may cover one or more AI systems.
evidence_span: The AI Office and the Member States shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct

statement_summary: The Commission shall develop guidelines on the practical implementation of the Regulation (Articles 8 to 15 and 25, prohibited practices, substantial modification, Article 50 transparency, relationship with Annex I and other Union law, the definition of an AI system), paying particular attention to SMEs, local public authorities and affected sectors and taking due account of the state of the art and relevant standards, and shall update guidelines at the request of the Member States or the AI Office or on its own initiative when deemed necessary.
evidence_span: The Commission shall develop guidelines on the practical implementation of this Regulation

statement_summary: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in the listed Articles is conferred on the Commission for five years from 1 August 2024, tacitly extended for periods of identical duration unless the European Parliament or the Council opposes, may be revoked at any time by the European Parliament or the Council without affecting delegated acts already in force, and a delegated act enters into force only if neither the European Parliament nor the Council has objected within three months of notification (extendable by three months).
evidence_span: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission

statement_summary: The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period and shall notify each delegated act simultaneously to the European Parliament and to the Council as soon as it adopts it.
evidence_span: The Commission shall draw up a report in respect of the delegation of power not later than nine months before the end of the five-year period

statement_summary: Before adopting a delegated act the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State in accordance with the principles of the Interinstitutional Agreement of 13 April 2016 on Better Law-Making.
evidence_span: the Commission shall consult experts designated by each Member State

statement_summary: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011, and where reference is made to Article 98(2) Article 5 of that Regulation applies.
evidence_span: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee

statement_summary: Member States shall lay down rules on penalties and other enforcement measures applicable to infringements by operators, which may include warnings and non-monetary measures, take all measures necessary to ensure proper and effective implementation taking into account the guidelines of Article 96, ensure penalties are effective, proportionate and dissuasive and take SME interests into account; they shall notify the rules to the Commission without delay and at the latest by the date of entry into application, lay down rules on the extent to which administrative fines may be imposed on public authorities and bodies, and report annually to the Commission on fines issued and related litigation.
evidence_span: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties and other enforcement measures

statement_summary: Non-compliance with the Article 5 prohibitions is subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover; non-compliance with the obligations of providers, authorised representatives, importers, distributors, deployers, notified bodies and the Article 50 transparency obligations to fines of up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3 %; supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities to fines of up to EUR 7 500 000 or 1 %; for SMEs the lower amount applies.
evidence_span: Non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5 shall be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 35 000 000

statement_summary: In deciding on an administrative fine and its amount all relevant circumstances shall be taken into account and regard given to listed factors; depending on the legal system the fines may be imposed by competent national courts or by other bodies with equivalent effect; the exercise of powers is subject to appropriate procedural safeguards including effective judicial remedies and due process.
evidence_span: the rules on administrative fines may be applied in such a manner that the fines are imposed by competent national courts or by other bodies

statement_summary: The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies falling within the scope of the Regulation (up to EUR 1 500 000 for non-compliance with Article 5 and up to EUR 750 000 for other requirements) taking into account listed factors, after giving the entity the opportunity to be heard and respecting the rights of defence including access to the file, with funds contributing to the general budget of the Union, and shall notify the Commission annually of fines imposed and related litigation.
evidence_span: The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies falling within the scope of this Regulation

statement_summary: The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of annual total worldwide turnover or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher, when it finds that the provider intentionally or negligently infringed relevant provisions, failed to comply with a request for a document or information under Article 91 or supplied incorrect, incomplete or misleading information, failed to comply with a measure requested under Article 93 or failed to give access for an evaluation under Article 92, having regard to nature, gravity and duration and taking into account commitments under Article 93(3) or codes of practice, after communicating preliminary findings and giving the provider an opportunity to be heard.
evidence_span: The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover

statement_summary: Information on fines imposed shall be communicated to the Board as appropriate; the Court of Justice of the European Union has unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the Commission fixing a fine and may cancel, reduce or increase the fine; the Commission shall adopt implementing acts containing detailed arrangements and procedural safeguards for proceedings under the examination procedure of Article 98(2).
evidence_span: The Court of Justice of the European Union shall have unlimited jurisdiction to review decisions of the Commission fixing a fine under this Article

statement_summary: Without prejudice to Article 5, AI systems which are components of the large-scale IT systems established by the legal acts listed in Annex X and placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 shall be brought into compliance by 31 December 2030, and the requirements shall be taken into account in the evaluation of each such large-scale IT system; the party bound is not named.

statement_summary: Without prejudice to Article 5, the Regulation applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026 only if, as from that date, the systems are subject to significant changes in their designs, and the providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities shall take the necessary steps to comply by 2 August 2030.

statement_summary: The Commission shall assess annually the need to amend Annex III and Article 5 and report findings to the European Parliament and the Council, evaluate and report by 2 August 2028 and every four years on listed matters, submit by 2 August 2029 and every four years a public report on evaluation and review including the structure of enforcement and the possible need for a Union agency with proposals where appropriate, evaluate the functioning of the AI Office by 2 August 2028, report on standardisation deliverables on energy-efficient development of general-purpose AI models, evaluate voluntary codes of conduct, assess enforcement by 2 August 2031 and report to the European Parliament, the Council and the European Economic and Social Committee, taking into account positions of the Board, the European Parliament and the Council, with information provided by the Board, Member States and national competent authorities on request, and the AI Office shall develop an objective and participative methodology for risk-level evaluation.

statement_summary: The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day following its publication in the Official Journal and applies from 2 August 2026, except that Chapters I and II apply from 2 February 2025, Chapter III Section 4, Chapter V, Chapter VII, Chapter XII and Article 78 apply from 2 August 2025 with the exception of Article 101, and Article 6(1) and the corresponding obligations apply from 2 August 2027.

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems intended to be used as safety components in the management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or the supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems used in education and vocational training to determine access, admission or assignment, evaluate learning outcomes, assess the appropriate level of education or monitor prohibited behaviour of students during tests.
evidence_span: AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at all levels

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems used in employment and workers management for recruitment or selection, for decisions on terms of work-related relationships, promotion or termination, task allocation based on behaviour or traits, and monitoring and evaluation of performance.
evidence_span: AI systems intended to be used for the recruitment or selection of natural persons

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems used by or on behalf of public authorities to evaluate eligibility for essential public assistance benefits and services, to evaluate creditworthiness (except fraud detection), for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance, and to evaluate and classify emergency calls and dispatch emergency first response services.
evidence_span: AI systems intended to be used by public authorities or on behalf of public authorities to evaluate the eligibility of natural persons for essential public assistance benefits and services

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of them, to assess the risk of becoming a victim of crime, as polygraphs, to evaluate the reliability of evidence, to assess the risk of offending or re-offending not solely on profiling, and for profiling in the course of detection, investigation or prosecution of criminal offences; profiling is defined by reference to Directive (EU) 2016/680.
evidence_span: AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of law enforcement authorities, or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in support of law enforcement authorities or on their behalf to assess the risk of a natural person becoming the victim of criminal offences

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies in migration, asylum and border control management as polygraphs, to assess security, irregular migration or health risks, to assist examination of asylum, visa and residence permit applications, and to detect, recognise or identify natural persons (except verification of travel documents).
evidence_span: AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of competent public authorities or by Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies as polygraphs or similar tools

statement_summary: Annex III lists as high-risk AI systems intended to be used by or on behalf of a judicial authority to assist in researching and interpreting facts and law or in alternative dispute resolution, and systems intended to influence the outcome of an election or referendum or voting behaviour (excluding tools to which natural persons are not directly exposed).
evidence_span: AI systems intended to be used by a judicial authority or on their behalf to assist a judicial authority in researching and interpreting facts and the law

statement_summary: The conformity assessment procedure based on internal control consists of the provider verifying that the quality management system complies with Article 17, examining the technical documentation to assess compliance with the Section 2 requirements and verifying that the design and development process and post-market monitoring are consistent with the technical documentation.
evidence_span: The provider verifies that the established quality management system is in compliance with the requirements of Article 17

statement_summary: Conformity assessment based on an assessment of the quality management system and of the technical documentation proceeds through points 2 to 5: the approved quality management system under Article 17 is examined under point 3 and subject to surveillance under point 5, and the technical documentation is examined under point 4.
evidence_span: Conformity based on an assessment of the quality management system and an assessment of the technical documentation is the conformity assessment procedure based on points 2 to 5

statement_summary: The provider applies to the notified body with a prescribed application including a declaration that no other application has been lodged; the notified body assesses the quality management system against Article 17, notifies the provider or its authorised representative of the conclusions and reasoned decision, and examines intended changes notified by the provider and notifies its decision; the provider continues to implement and maintain the approved quality management system.
evidence_span: The quality management system shall be assessed by the notified body, which shall determine whether it satisfies the requirements referred to in Article 17

statement_summary: The provider lodges an application with a notified body of its choice for assessment of the technical documentation with a prescribed content and declaration; the notified body examines the technical documentation with full access to the training, validation and testing data sets, may require further evidence or tests, carries out tests itself if not satisfied, may be granted access to training and trained models upon a reasoned request subject to Union law on intellectual property and trade secrets, notifies its decision with conclusions and reasoned assessment decision to the provider or its authorised representative, issues a Union technical documentation assessment certificate where the system conforms or refuses it with detailed reasons, and assesses changes notified by the provider, issuing a supplement where changes are approved.
evidence_span: an application with a notified body of their choice shall be lodged by the provider for the assessment of the technical documentation

statement_summary: The notified body carries out surveillance to make sure the provider complies with the approved quality management system: the provider allows the notified body to access the premises where design, development and testing take place and shares all necessary information, and the notified body carries out periodic audits, provides the provider with an audit report and may carry out additional tests of certified AI systems.
evidence_span: The purpose of the surveillance carried out by the notified body referred to in Point 3 is to make sure that the provider duly complies with the terms and conditions of the approved quality management system

statement_summary: Annex VIII Section A states the information to be provided and kept up to date for high-risk AI systems registered under Article 49(1): provider, submitting person and authorised representative details, trade name and identification, intended purpose and components, information used and operating logic, status, notified body certificate details and copy, Member States of availability, a copy of the EU declaration of conformity, electronic instructions for use (not for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control systems) and an optional URL.
